## Summary
Two changes that ride together because the workflow consumes secrets that bootstrap now seeds:

### 1. `.github/workflows/deploy-platform.yml`
Direct kubectl/helm bootstrap of in-cluster data plane and analytics + recommendations Helm releases. No ArgoCD (free-tier capacity), no Elasticsearch:
- `analytics` chart deployed with `kafkaEsConsumer.enabled=false`
- `recommendations` chart deployed with `configDynamic.ELASTICSEARCH_URL=""`

### 2. `scripts/bootstrap-aws.sh` — phase 2.5: sync GitHub secrets
Reads terraform outputs and pushes via `gh secret set` so the deploy workflows in both repos don't need manual rotation after every fresh apply:
- → `videostreamingplatform`: S3_VIDEOS_BUCKET, REDIS_ENDPOINT, RDS_ENDPOINT, RDS_MASTER_USER_SECRET_ARN, CDN_DISTRIBUTION_ID, IRSA_METADATA_ROLE_ARN, IRSA_DATA_ROLE_ARN, KAFKA_BROKERS, OPENSEARCH_ENDPOINT
- → `videostreamingplatform-infra`: ANALYTICS_IRSA_ROLE_ARN, RECOMMENDATIONS_IRSA_ROLE_ARN

Toggle with `--skip-github-secrets` or run alone via `--only-github-secrets`. Best-effort: warns and continues on missing tf output / no gh auth / repo not visible.

author: akshitbeniwal
body:
Wraps the main upload loop in a try/except that catches transient network errors from both the XNAT server and the S3-compatible store backends:

- requests.exceptions.ConnectionError
- requests.exceptions.ConnectTimeout
- requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout
- xnat.exceptions.XNATResponseError
- botocore.exceptions.EndpointConnectionError
- botocore.exceptions.ConnectTimeoutError
- botocore.exceptions.ReadTimeoutError

Previously, any transient network error would raise an unhandled exception and crash the process.

For Kubernetes deployments this causes the container to restart via the kubelet, producing spurious restart events log noise, and brief service interruptions.

In loop mode (--loop >= 0), transient errors are now logged and the loop continues at the next interval. In one-shot mode, the exception is re-raised so callers see the failure.

author: esimkowitz
body:
## Summary

Rolls up the three failing dependabot PRs (#322, #324, #326) into one coherent upgrade and fixes the underlying CI failures.

- `digest`, `md-5`, `sha1`, `sha2`: 0.10 → 0.11
- `uuid`: 1.20 → 1.23.1
- New direct dep `getrandom_04 = { package = "getrandom", version = "0.4", optional = true }`, mirroring the existing `getrandom_02` pattern, with `web` feature flipping its `wasm_js` backend.

## Why the dependabot PRs failed

- **#324 / #326 (md-5, digest)** — bumping a single RustCrypto crate left two majors of `digest` in the graph. `DynDigest` trait impls don't unify across crate versions, so `Box::<md5::Md5>::default() as Box<dyn DynDigest>` fails to type-check. Bumping the whole RustCrypto family (digest + md-5 + sha1 + sha2) together restores a single `digest` 0.11 in the tree.
- **#322 (uuid 1.23.1)** — uuid 1.23 transitively pulls `getrandom 0.4` (via `uuid-rng-internal` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`). `getrandom 0.4` requires opting into the `wasm_js` backend on that target; without the feature enabled the build fails with `compile_error!("The wasm32-unknown-unknown targets are not supported by default…")`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` (default/desktop) — clean
- [x] `cargo check --no-default-features --features web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt -- --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D clippy::style -D clippy::complexity -D clippy::perf` — clean
- [x] `dx build --platform web --release` — Rust compilation through wasm-bindgen succeeds
- [ ] CI green on all three checks (Format Check, Clippy, Build)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Dependency upgrades touch hashing and RNG/UUID generation and add a new wasm-specific `getrandom` path, which could affect runtime behavior across targets despite being mostly version bumps.
> 
> **Overview**
> Upgrades the RustCrypto hashing dependency set (`digest`, `md-5`, `sha1`, `sha2`) from `0.10` to `0.11` to keep `DynDigest` consumers on a single major version.
> 
> Bumps `uuid` from `1.20` to `1.23` and updates the `web` feature to optionally enable `getrandom 0.4`’s `wasm_js` backend via a new `getrandom_04` dependency, with corresponding `Cargo.lock` refresh (new/updated transitive crates like `wasip3`, `wit-bindgen` updates, etc.).

author: kumarmanusaraswat
body:
## What I built
- A fully functional AI chatbot with:
  - Node.js + Express backend exposing a `/chat` route
  - Vanilla JavaScript frontend with chat UI (input box, send button, conversation display)
  - Conversation context handled via a `messages` array passed on every request

## How it works
- Frontend sends `POST /chat` to the backend with the full `messages` history (user + assistant messages).
- Backend reads `process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from `.env` and calls the OpenRouter Chat Completions API with the same `messages` array.
- The OpenRouter response is returned to the frontend, which appends it to the chat as an `assistant` message.
- Conversation history is maintained entirely on the frontend, so every new request includes the previous turns.

## Security and API keys
- API key is stored only in `backend/.env` and loaded via `process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
- `.env` is listed in `.gitignore`, so it is never committed to Git.
- The frontend never calls OpenRouter directly and never has the API key in its code or in the browser.

## Deployment
- **Frontend (live URL):** `https://your-frontend-url-here`
- **Backend (live URL):** `https://your-backend-url-here`

## Testing done
- Started backend locally with `npm start` inside `backend/`.
- Opened `frontend/index.html` in the browser.
- Asked: “What is JavaScript?” → got an explanation.
- Follow-up: “Can you give me an example of that?” → got a JavaScript-based example, confirming context is working.

## Checklist
- [x] `/chat` route implemented and calling OpenRouter
- [x] API key only in `.env`, not committed
- [x] Frontend uses backend `/chat` endpoint only
- [x] Conversation context maintained across messages
- [x] Backend deployed to Render
- [x] Frontend deployed to Netlify

author: myselflokendra
body:
## Bug Fixes

### ✅ Options trades not downloading to CSV
`exportTransactionsCSV` was called with `[]` for options in both Individual and IRA pipelines. Fixed to pass `data.optionsOrders`.

### ✅ Options Sheets sync used wrong fields
`option_type`, `strike_price`, `expiration_date` and execution price are inside `order.legs[0]`, not top-level. Fixed to read from `legs[0]` and compute weighted-average price from `leg.executions[]`.

### ✅ Date off by one
`formatDate()` used `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` which is parsed as UTC midnight. In US timezones (UTC-7/8) this shifts the day back by one. Fixed to parse ISO date-only strings as local date parts directly (same approach already used in `background.js`).

### ✅ Blank rows in stock CSV
Filter changed from `state=filled OR qty>0` to `state=filled AND qty>0`. Also added `.filter(r => r.Symbol !== "")` to drop rows where instrument URL lookup returned nothing.

### ✅ Amount Deposited returning empty
`normalizeDeposits()` filtered `unified_transfers` by exact `account_number` match, but the paymenthub API may use UUID-style account IDs. Now tries: exact match → substring match → fallback to all transfers (with console warning). Better than silently producing an empty CSV.

## New Features

### ✅ Sheets Account dropdown
Dropdown in the panel (visible when Sync is enabled) selects between:
- **Deepika — Production**
- **Lokendra — Production**
- **Lokendra — Test**

`background.js` reads the `sheetsOwner` key from the sync message and picks the right spreadsheet ID from `config.js`. Metadata cache is cleared on each switch.

### ✅ Download CSV on/off toggle
New toggle switch in the footer. When off, data is still fetched and synced to Sheets (if enabled) but no files are downloaded. All exporter functions accept a `downloadEnabled` parameter.

## Other
- README fully rewritten with feature table, CSV schema, project structure, Sheets column layout
- `config.js` now holds all 3 spreadsheet IDs in `googleSheets.accounts` map

## Test Plan
- [ ] Rebuild: `node build.js` → no errors
- [ ] Load unpacked `dist/` in Chrome
- [ ] Navigate to robinhood.com/account/investing
- [ ] Enable Options in Individual → verify `individual_orders.csv` contains option rows with Entity=Option
- [ ] Check dates in CSV match Robinhood UI (no off-by-one)

- [ ] Check Amount Deposited CSV — should have data even if account ID format differs
- [ ] Toggle "Download CSV" off → no files downloaded, Sheets sync still works

- Adds a hold-`Ctrl` sneak mode in Maze at 75% normal walk speed (`12` vs `16`).
- Keeps `LeftShift` sprint, door, and tool sound stimulus behavior unchanged.
- Makes sneak server-authoritative, sprint/sneak mutually exclusive, and silent by not reporting sound stimulus on sneak start/stop.

## Why This Lives In maze + shared movement

- The player input and HUD are Maze-local, but the movement mode and locomotion summary are shared runtime/gameplay seams used by place services and deterministic tests.
- No cross-place teleport/session contract shape changes are introduced.

## Scope

- `Gameplay.ControlState.Mode` adds `Sneak` plus `requestSneakStart` / `requestSneakStop`.
- `FormalLocomotion` adds `SneakWalkSpeed = 12` and surfaces `Mode = "Sneak"` for HUD/status.
- Maze client sends `RequestSneakStart` / `RequestSneakStop` for `LeftControl` and `RightControl`.
- Maze server applies sneak mode, clears it during movement cleanup, and does not report predator sound for sneak.

#### Why I did it

Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22389

SONiC builds FRR with `-Ppkg.frr.nortrlib`, which passes `--disable-rpki` to FRR's configure script and suppresses the `frr-rpki-rtrlib` package entirely. This means RPKI prefix validation is unavailable even though FRR's source tree contains the complete implementation. The `nortrlib` flag was introduced in PR #2454 (2019) when FRR was upgraded to 6.0.2, likely due to missing `librtr-dev` in the build environment at the time, and has been carried forward through every subsequent FRR upgrade without re-evaluation. Since Debian 12 (bookworm) ships `librtr-dev` 0.8.0 and the cross-build slave already installs it, the flag is no longer necessary.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it
* Add `INCLUDE_FRR_RPKI` build toggle in `rules/config` (default `y`) with full build system plumbing (`Makefile.work` passthrough, `slave.mk` export and `$(info)` diagnostic)
* Conditionally remove the `nortrlib` profile, register the `frr-rpki-rtrlib` .deb package, and install it in `docker-fpm-frr`
* Register `frr_rpki` FEATURE in `init_cfg.json.j2` (default state `disabled`) and add FEATURE-gated `-M rpki` module loading in bgpd's supervisord config with correct `and`/`or` parenthesization
* Skip `frr_rpki` in container health checkers (same pattern as `frr_bmp`)

#### How to verify it
1. Build with default config and verify `frr-rpki-rtrlib_*.deb` is produced and installed in `docker-fpm-frr`
2. Set `INCLUDE_FRR_RPKI = n` in `rules/config` and verify the build reverts to the original behavior (no RPKI package)
3. On a running image, enable via `config feature state frr_rpki enabled`, restart bgp container, and confirm `rpki` command is available in vtysh

author: jasontofte
body:
## Summary

PR 2 of the Phase 8 fix-up sweep. Closes 2 High findings from the final review gate (`fw-review-types` HIGH-1 and HIGH-2):

- **H-4** — All six parsers (amcache, appcompat, bam, prefetch, sysmon, userassist) now source their `_FAMILY` constant from `sanctum.families.FAMILY_*` instead of hardcoded string literals. A typo in any of those literals would have silently produced a string that failed family-gate corroboration without raising. `families.py` already exposes the `Final`-typed constants; this PR just consumes them.
- **H-5** — `bam.py` introduces `SidStatus = Literal[...]` for the closed set of SID classification labels (`system_account`, `builtin_admin`, `builtin_guest`, `builtin_default`, `builtin_wdag`, `orphan_oobe`, `user_unverified`). `_WELLKNOWN_SYSTEM_SIDS`, `_USER_RID_NAMED`, `_DROP_STATUSES`, `_classify_sid`, and the `_events_from_sid_subkey` / `_build_event_from_value` signatures all flow through that type.

## Why this matters

Without `SidStatus`, `_DROP_STATUSES = frozenset({\"orphan_oobe\"})` is just a string set — a typo would silently demote the OOBE drop rule to a no-op and let `defaultuser0` events vote into the family-corroboration gate. That's exactly the silent-failure mode the family gate is designed to prevent. The Literal turns that typo from a runtime no-op into a mypy error, so the type system now enforces the OOBE-drop invariant.

Same logic for the `_FAMILY` strings: a typo (`\"AppCmpat\"` etc.) would not raise at parse time but would fail family-gate corroboration silently. Importing from `sanctum.families` makes the family set a typed, single-source-of-truth dependency.

## Files changed

- `src/sanctum/parsers/amcache.py` — `FAMILY_APPCOMPAT`
- `src/sanctum/parsers/appcompat.py` — `FAMILY_APPCOMPAT`
- `src/sanctum/parsers/bam.py` — `FAMILY_BACKGROUND_SERVICE` + `SidStatus` Literal
- `src/sanctum/parsers/prefetch.py` — `FAMILY_SYSMAIN`
- `src/sanctum/parsers/sysmon.py` — `FAMILY_KERNEL_ETW`
- `src/sanctum/parsers/userassist.py` — `FAMILY_EXPLORER_NTUSER`

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` — 251 pass, 6 skip (rig-baseline fixtures pre-existing). No regressions.
- [x] `mypy src/sanctum/parsers/bam.py` — 14 pre-existing untyped-call / missing-stubs errors (regipy, python-evtx, windowsprefetch); zero new errors from `SidStatus` flow.
- [x] `ruff check src/sanctum/parsers/` — clean.
- [x] No hardcoded `family=\"...\"` literals remain in `src/sanctum/parsers/`.

## Sequencing

Independent of #34 — branched off `origin/main`, not stacked. Per the project's stacked-PR-merge-hazard policy, all five Phase 8 fix-ups go in as parallel PRs off main.

author: indrajit96
body:
#### Overview:

Add SGLang backend support for the OpenAI-compatible `n` field on top of PR #8744.
This PR is intentionally scoped to SGLang only. The shared OpenAI/Rust response contract and vLLM plumbing are handled in the parent PR.

#### WHY:

PR #8744 adds the shared Dynamo contract for carrying multiple OpenAI choices by preserving each backend output `index`.

  SGLang already supports generating multiple output sequences through `n`; its OpenAI chat API accepts OpenAI Chat Completions parameters, and its sampling docs define `n` as the number of output sequences to generate per request.

  References:
  - SGLang OpenAI chat parameters: https://docs.sglang.io/docs/basic_usage/openai_api_completions
  - SGLang `SamplingParams.n`: https://docs.sglang.io/docs/basic_usage/sampling_params

  Without this SGLang-specific plumbing, Dynamo can pass through the parent contract but SGLang chunks may still collapse into choice `0`, or interleaved `n > 1` streams can compute text/logprob deltas using the wrong choice state.


#### Details:

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/llm_engine.py`
    - Passes `n` into SGLang sampling params for direct SGLang engine requests.
    - Preserves SGLang’s streamed output `index` so the parent OpenAI response layer can keep choices separate.
    - Defaults missing indexes to `0` for legacy / `n=1` chunks.

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/decode_handler.py`
    - Passes `n` through both tokenized and SGLang-tokenizer request paths.
    - Preserves `index` on token-mode chunks.
    - Tracks cumulative output logprob offsets per choice index instead of globally.
    - Tracks cumulative text offsets per choice index for text streaming, since SGLang text chunks are cumulative and `n > 1` choices can be interleaved.

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/prefill_handler.py`
    - Passes `n` into SGLang sampling params for disaggregated prefill requests.

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/multimodal/worker_handler.py`
    - Passes `n` for multimodal SGLang requests.
    - Preserves the output choice `index` in multimodal streams.

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/tests/test_sglang_decode_handler.py`
    - Adds unit coverage that `n` is included in sampling params.
    - Adds regression coverage for per-choice logprob cursor tracking.
    - Adds regression coverage for per-choice cumulative text delta tracking.

  - `tests/serve/test_sglang.py`
    - Adds pre-merge serve coverage that a chat request with `n=2` returns two choices.


#### Where should the reviewer start?

  Start with:

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/decode_handler.py`

  That file contains the main streaming behavior that can break when `n > 1` choices are interleaved.

  Then review:

  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/llm_engine.py`
  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/multimodal/worker_handler.py`
  - `components/src/dynamo/sglang/tests/test_sglang_decode_handler.py`
  - `tests/serve/test_sglang.py`

author: htalat
body:
## Summary

Different repos need different shipping flows — solo direct-pushes, team PRs, sensitive draft-PRs. Rather than enumerate strategies in tpm's frontmatter and drift from each repo's actual conventions, point the agent at the repo's own workflow doc and get out of the way.

### What ships

1. **Optional `workflow:` field** on project + task frontmatter (string path, relative to repo root). Loader needs no change — frontmatter is already `Record<string, unknown>`, so `data.workflow` falls out for free. The project template gets a commented placeholder so the field is discoverable without being mandatory.

2. **`tpm context` surfaces the chain.** A new `Workflow:` line in the briefing whenever the field is set, and the working agreement always names the resolution chain the agent follows after `cd`-ing into `repo.local`:
   - `workflow:` pointer if set, else `AGENTS.md`, else `CLAUDE.md`, else ask before each shipping step.

3. **SKILL.md `<task>` mode** learns step 5 (resolve the workflow doc) and step 8 (ship per the doc; for `type: pr` tasks the default is leave in-progress until the PR merges, then `/tpm done`).

### Dogfood

tpm's own `AGENTS.md` gets a `## Workflow` section describing the rules this PR was authored under: `npm test` gates commits, doc-only goes direct to `main`, behavior changes go via PR, PR-typed tasks close after merge.

### Why not strategies in tpm's frontmatter

The original draft of #2 enumerated `flow: pr | direct-push | draft-pr | commit-only | ask`. Re-shaped during `/tpm discuss`: workflow is repo-specific knowledge that already wants to live in `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code already auto-loads CLAUDE.md; agents already read AGENTS.md by convention). Encoding strategies in tpm would duplicate, drift, and constrain the doc form. The pointer field handles non-standard layouts; the convention covers everything else.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 107 tests pass (3 new in `context.test.ts` covering: workflow surfaces in briefing, task-level overrides project-level, absent workflow falls back to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md hint)
- [x] `tpm context 002-configurable-flow` end-to-end smoke confirms the working agreement names the fallback chain when no `workflow:` is set
- [ ] After merge: re-run a small `/tpm <task>` in tpm and confirm the agent reads `AGENTS.md`, follows it, and (for a PR-typed task) leaves the task `in-progress` post-PR

author: pazerop
body:
## Summary

This PR adds functionality to automatically create external Docker networks, named volumes, and bind-mount source directories before running `docker compose up`. This eliminates first-deploy failures when a compose file references shared infrastructure that doesn't yet exist.

## Key Changes

- **New `prerequisites.go` module** in `internal/compose/`:
  - `ExternalNetworks()` - extracts networks marked with `external: true` from compose YAML
  - `ExternalVolumes()` - extracts volumes marked with `external: true` from compose YAML
  - `BindMountSources()` - extracts absolute host paths used as bind-mount sources
  - `NetworkInspect()`, `NetworkCreate()` - check and create Docker networks
  - `VolumeInspect()`, `VolumeCreate()` - check and create Docker volumes
  - Helper functions for YAML parsing and Docker error detection

- **Runner enhancements** in `internal/runner/runner.go`:
  - Added three new config flags: `EnsureNetworks`, `EnsureBindMounts`, `EnsureNamedVolumes`
  - `ensureNetworks()` - creates missing external networks before `compose up`
  - `ensureNamedVolumes()` - creates missing external volumes before `compose up`
  - `ensureBindMounts()` - creates missing bind-mount source directories with `mkdir -p`
  - Integration into `Tick()` to run prerequisite checks before reconciliation

- **CLI updates** in `cmd/run.go` and `cmd/apply.go`:
  - Added three new boolean flags (all default to `true`)
  - Flags are wired through to the runner configuration

- **Docker interface expansion** in `internal/compose/compose.go`:
  - Added `networkInspect()`, `networkCreate()`, `volumeInspect()`, `volumeCreate()` to runner interface
  - Implemented with real Docker CLI calls via `docker network/volume inspect/create`

- **Comprehensive test coverage**:
  - `prerequisites_test.go` - 16 new tests covering YAML parsing, network/volume inspection, and creation
  - `runner_test.go` - 4 new integration tests verifying prerequisite creation behavior
  - Updated fake implementations to support the new operations

- **Documentation** in `README.md`:
  - Added flag descriptions for the three new ensure options
  - New "Prerequisite resources" section explaining the feature and use cases

## Implementation Details

- YAML parsing uses the existing `yaml.Node` tree structure for efficient extraction
- Deduplication of bind-mount sources across multiple services
- Graceful error handling - failures to create prerequisites log warnings but don't block `compose up`
- Docker "not found" errors are distinguished from other failures (e.g., daemon unreachable)
- All three ensure features are independently toggleable and default to enabled

author: biboylin
body:
## Summary

Adds a POWER message class to the STM32 coprocessor protocol and maps 5V enable/disable commands to the existing IP5306 KEY control path.

This PR is scoped to the current STM32 Debug bring-up firmware. The ESP32 bench is powered from USB-C, so the IP5306 path controls only the STM32-side 5V rail for servos and WS2812 LEDs; it does not power-cycle the ESP32 itself.

## Changes

- Adds `COPROC_MSG_CLASS_POWER` with `POWER_5V_ENABLE` and `POWER_5V_DISABLE`.
- Advertises the new power capability in `HELLO_RSP`.
- Handles POWER frames in `CoprocRuntime` with ACK/NACK behavior and runtime observations.
- Routes enable to `IP5306_Key_ShortPress()` and disable to `IP5306_Key_DoubleShortPress()`.
- Keeps `ip5306_on` / `ip5306_off` CLI behavior aligned with the same `App_SetPower5V()` entrypoint.
- Adds a Debug-firmware-only POWER enable servo probe: after 5V enable, delay 600 ms, then drive Servo1 to 70 deg and Servo2 to 110 deg so the bench can be visually inspected.
- Documents the real bench power boundary and calls out that the servo probe is a Debug validation aid, not a formal App firmware behavior.
- Adds host coverage for the POWER runtime path.

## Validation

- `cmake --build --preset Debug`
- STM32 flashed via ST-Link, OpenOCD `Verified OK`
- Manual COM56 CLI check after flashing Debug firmware:
  - `ip5306_on`
  - observed `POWER5V SERVO PROBE`
  - `Servo1 : OK angle=70 deg pulse=1277 us`
  - `Servo2 : OK angle=110 deg pulse=1722 us`
- 20-cycle 5V HIL toggle on COM37/COM56:
  - `ip5306_off`: 20/20
  - `ip5306_on`: 20/20
  - off actions: 20/20
  - on actions: 20/20
  - STM32 log lines: 236
  - ESP32 log lines: 156
- Previous host/runtime checks:
  - `C:\Espressif\tools\cmake\3.24.0\bin\cmake.exe --build build\HostDebug`
  - `build\HostDebug\Debug\coproc_host_tests.exe`

## Notes

- ESP32 is expected to remain online after `POWER_5V_DISABLE` because its board power is USB-C, not the IP5306-controlled 5V rail.
- The 610-second stress run kept the link healthy (`ack_timeout_count=0`, `crc_error_count=0`, `reconnect_count=0`) but the current evaluator expects `MCU_OBS evt=stress_stats`; the ESP32 firmware emitted `MCU_OBS evt=stats`, so that specific automatic stress verdict remains an evaluator/event-name mismatch rather than a POWER link failure.
- Protocol baseline: `Ro-In-AI/WatcheRobot-Firmware@proto/v2.0.0-stm32-align-20260416`.

author: lestrrat
body:
The built-in importers for stdlib raw key types (rsa, ecdsa, ed25519, ecdh — value and pointer forms — plus \`[]byte\`) are claimed by jwk and dispatched through the \`importBuiltinKey\` fast path before the user-extensible \`keyImporters\` map is consulted. A caller passing one of those types to \`RegisterKeyImporter\` previously hit the generic "already registered; call UnregisterKeyImporter first" message — misleading because even after Unregister + Register, the fast-path switch would still shadow the registration.

This change tracks the built-in set explicitly:

- \`RegisterKeyImporter\` returns \`built-in importers cannot be overridden\` for those types.
- \`UnregisterKeyImporter\` is a silent no-op for them; the importer remains functional after the call.
- Godoc on \`RegisterKeyImporter\` and \`UnregisterKeyImporter\` spells out the off-limits list and points at wrapper types as the supported extension path.

Test added at \`jwk/convert_test.go:TestRegisterKeyImporterRejectsBuiltinTypes\`.

author: pjm17971
body:
## Summary

Second PR of the v0.10 wave. Closes the dashboard agent's "missing terminal" friction from v0.9.0 round-2 feedback:

> A terminal that materializes back to a `Map<partitionKey, TimeSeries<R>>` directly from the partition view — `.toMap()` or `.split()` — would close the loop. Currently `apply` flattens to one `TimeSeries`; sometimes you want them apart.
> — dashboard agent feedback

Replaces the awkward `.collect().groupBy(col, fn)` chain that dashboard code was using to land on `Map<host, points[]>`.

## API

```ts
toMap(): Map<string, TimeSeries<S>>;
toMap<R extends SeriesSchema>(
  transform: (group: TimeSeries<S>) => TimeSeries<R>,
): Map<string, TimeSeries<R>>;
toMap<R>(transform: (group: TimeSeries<S>) => R): Map<string, R>;
```

Three overloads cover the common shapes — bare per-partition `TimeSeries`, transform that returns a `TimeSeries<R>` (e.g. `g.diff('cpu')`), and transform that returns arbitrary `R` (e.g. `g.toPoints()`).

```ts
// Per-host event lookup
const byHost = events.partitionBy('host').toMap();
const apiEvents = byHost.get('api-1');

// One-shot per-partition shape change for charting
const points = events.partitionBy('host').toMap((g) => g.toPoints());
for (const [host, rows] of points) chart.addSeries(host, rows);

// Composite partition
const byHostRegion = events.partitionBy(['host', 'region']).toMap();
const apiEu = byHostRegion.get('["api-1","eu"]');
```

## Refactor

Extracted `compositeKey` and bucket-building from `applyToSource` into shared static helpers (`partitionKeyOf`, `bucketByPartition`) so both `apply()` and `toMap()` use the same encoder — a fix to one fixes both.

## Performance (per CLAUDE.md perf-check policy)

**Complexity:** O(N + T) — single bucketing pass over events, per-bucket `TimeSeries.fromEvents` (timsort linear on already-sorted input), Map iteration O(B). Asymptotically optimal.

**Benchmark** (Apple Silicon, Node 24, see `scripts/perf-partitioned-toMap.mjs`):

| Scenario                                           | Time    |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------: |
| 100k events × 10 hosts → `toMap()`                 |  5.2 ms |
| 100k events × 10 hosts → `toMap(g => g.toPoints())` | 33.0 ms |
| 100k events × 10 hosts → `.collect().groupBy(...)` | 108 ms  |
| 100k events × 1 host  → `toMap()`                  |  3.0 ms |
| 100k events × 1000 hosts → `toMap()`               |  7.4 ms |

**Headline: `toMap(g => g.toPoints())` is 3.3× faster than the `.collect().groupBy(...)` chain it replaces** at 100k events × 10 hosts. ~75 ms saved per dashboard refresh.

Bare `toMap` scales near-flat with partition cardinality (5 ms at 10 hosts, 7 ms at 1000 hosts) — Map insertion is O(1) per event.

## Tests

14 new tests under `TimeSeries.partitionBy.toMap.test.ts`:
- **Basic shape** (5): one entry per partition, schema preserved, event order, empty source, iteration order
- **With transform** (4): TimeSeries-returning, arbitrary R, replaces-old-chain comparison, stateful op (diff)
- **Composite keys** (2): JSON encoding, no separator collisions
- **`undefined` as partition key value (regression)** (3) — closes the PR #80 review follow-up. Pins the leading-space sentinel for single-column, the no-collision-with-`'undefined'`-string guarantee, and the JSON `null` encoding for composite.

**868 core tests pass** (was 854, +14).

## Coming next in v0.10 (PR 3 of 3)

Typed `partitionBy('host', { groups: HOSTS as const })` — narrows the Map key to `typeof HOSTS[number]` instead of bare string. Mirrors the `pivotByGroup({ groups })` pattern.

- `observability.InstrumentAuthorizationProvider(name, provider)` wraps the existing `core.AuthorizationProvider` interface and emits `authorization.provider.operation` spans plus `gestaltd.authorization.provider.operation.*` metrics.
- `observability.InstrumentExternalCredentialProvider(name, provider)` wraps the existing `core.ExternalCredentialProvider` interface and emits `credential.provider.operation` spans plus `gestaltd.credential.provider.operation.*` metrics.
- `invocation.EffectiveCredentialBindingResolver` now accepts `context.Context` so credential binding and token resolution remain in the request trace tree: `ResolveEffectiveCredentialBinding(ctx, principal, providerName, connection, instance)`.

## Examples

- `POST /api/v1/agent/sessions/{id}/turns` now produces a trace tree with `agent.operation`, `agent.tool.resolve`, `catalog.operation.resolve`, `agent.run_metadata.write`, and `agent.provider.operation` spans.
- Agent provider calls emit metrics such as `gestaltd.agent.provider.operation.count{gestalt.agent.provider="managed", gestalt.agent.operation="create_turn"}`.
- Catalog resolution emits `gestaltd.catalog.operation.resolve.count{gestalt.provider="docs", gestalt.operation="search"}` and normalizes unresolved user-supplied operation names to `gestalt.operation="unknown"`.
- Provider-backed authorization emits `gestaltd.authorization.provider.evaluate.*` using the configured provider key in `gestalt.authorization.provider`.

## Notes

- Does not add GenAI semantic metrics or optional metric families.
- Keeps metric names under `gestaltd.*`; attributes remain under `gestalt.*`.
- Updates observability and provider-authoring docs for the new metric/span contract.

Close  #231 

## PR Description

### Title: [STORAGE] Fix Orphaned PartialRefundProposal Storage Cleanup

### Description

**Problem Statement:**
Partial refund proposals are stored per order ID and may survive even after an escrow is resolved, leading to orphaned storage that wastes space and increases state bloat over time.

**Root Cause:**
The `PartialRefundProposal` storage entries were only being cleaned up in the `accept_partial_refund` function, but not in other escrow finalization paths:
- Arbitrator dispute resolution (`resolve_dispute`)
- Expired dispute auto-resolution (`resolve_expired_dispute`)
- Proposal cancellation (no function existed)

**Solution Implemented:**

1. **Added `cancel_partial_refund` function** - Allows the original proposer to cancel their partial refund proposal, removing it from storage and enabling new proposals if needed.

2. **Enhanced `resolve_dispute`** - Added cleanup of any existing partial refund proposal when an arbitrator resolves a dispute.

3. **Enhanced `resolve_expired_dispute`** - Added cleanup of any existing partial refund proposal when an expired dispute is auto-resolved.

**Key Changes:**
- `src/lib.rs`: Added `cancel_partial_refund` function and proposal cleanup in dispute resolution functions
- Maintains existing behavior for `accept_partial_refund` (already cleaned up proposals)
- Follows CEI pattern (Checks-Effects-Interactions) for safe state management

**Acceptance Criteria Met:**
✅ Clear PartialRefundProposal storage on refund completion (existing)  
✅ Clear PartialRefundProposal storage on cancellation (new)  
✅ Clear PartialRefundProposal storage on escrow finalization (enhanced)

**Testing Approach:**
- Unit tests for `cancel_partial_refund` functionality
- Integration tests verifying cleanup in all dispute resolution paths
- Storage bloat prevention verification
- Regression testing to ensure no existing functionality is broken

**Impact:**
- Prevents indefinite storage growth from orphaned proposals
- Maintains clean contract state
- Improves long-term contract performance and cost efficiency
- No breaking changes to existing API

**Files Changed:**
- lib.rs

**Related Issues:**
- Closes storage optimization task for PartialRefundProposal orphaned entries

author: pha3idp344
body:
The aiBudgetGuard helper has been deployed for ~2 days but no edge function called recordAiSpend(). Without it the per-tier USD caps in the ai_spend_ledger migration are unenforced — a single bad actor (or a compromised anon key) can drain Claude/Gemini/Qwen credits unchecked.

Adds an env-gated feature flag (AI_BUDGET_GUARD_ENABLED, default OFF) so the wiring ships dark — no behaviour change until the flag is flipped, and flipping it back takes seconds if anything misbehaves.

Wired into the three most expensive AI surfaces:
  - claude-research        (Claude Haiku 4.5, ~$0.005/call, the priciest)
  - gemini-pro-analysis    (Gemini 1.5 Flash, ~$0.0005/call)
  - mulerouter-ai          (Qwen via MuleRouter, ~$0.001/call)

Each call ledgers the estimated cost via the existing record_ai_spend RPC BEFORE the upstream request, so the cap can never be exceeded by even one request. Identity is taken from the already-authenticated session (user.id from Supabase auth, or rl.userId returned by enforceAiRateLimit).

Also sanitises a leaky 500 in claude-research that was returning the raw Error.message from Anthropic API failures, leaking internal detail.

Rollout plan once enabled: caps are conservative on purpose (spark $0.50/mo, creator $2/mo, strategist $10/mo). Flip AI_BUDGET_GUARD_ENABLED=true in the edge-function env to start enforcing.

### Motivation
- Reduce high-volume 404 and hostile-probe noise by classifying and downgrading obvious scanner/probe traffic while preserving telemetry. 
- Prevent repeated runtime errors from missing resources (blog table, How-It-Works partial) and avoid unsafe JSON parsing in request handlers. 
- Avoid false-critical alerts from safe fallbacks (rate-limit auth resolution and CSRF blocks) and harden Solana RPC parsing to stop malformed responses from causing array-offset failures. 

### Description
- Added hostile-probe detection in `app/Config/Routes.php` to tag known scanner paths (e.g., `.env`, `.git`, `phpinfo.php`, `composer.*`, `docker-compose`) and log them as `notice` with `probe=true` while keeping genuine 404s at `error`. 
- Lowered severity of `[AUTH_RESOLUTION_FAILED]` in `app/Filters/RateLimitFilter.php` from `critical` to `warning` to reflect safe guest fallback behavior. 
- Lowered severity of `[CSRF][EXCEPTION]` in `app/Filters/CsrfDebugFilter.php` from `critical` to `warning` and retained targeted debug diagnostics. 
- Added table-existence guard and single-warning behaviour in `app/Models/BlogModel.php` so `blog_posts` absence returns safe empty/null responses instead of DB exceptions. 
- Fixed namespaced view include for How-It-Works navigation in `app/Modules/Blog/Views/HowItWorks/index.php` to stop invalid-file partial errors. 
- Hardened `WalletsController::delete()` in `app/Modules/User/Controllers/WalletsController.php` to check raw request body before calling `getJSON(true)` and to catch/notice invalid JSON while falling back to form/query params. 
- Tuned activation logging in `app/Controllers/AuthController.php` by changing missing-token logs from `notice` to `info` while preserving user redirect flow. 
- Hardened Solana parsing in `app/Libraries/MyMISolana.php` to defensively handle non-array or malformed `volume`/`volume_array` payloads and use controlled `warning` fallbacks. 
- Added an operations document at `docs/_aiops/log_repair_2026_04_29.md` summarizing the repairs. 

### Testing
- Ran `php -l` syntax checks for `app/Config/Routes.php`, `app/Filters/RateLimitFilter.php`, `app/Filters/CsrfDebugFilter.php`, `app/Models/BlogModel.php`, `app/Modules/User/Controllers/WalletsController.php`, and `app/Libraries/MyMISolana.php`, and all files reported "No syntax errors detected".

author: copilot
steve8708
body:
## Summary

Two unrelated fixes were bundled into this PR by concurrent agents. Both pass `pnpm prep` (494 tests).

### 1. Slack Block Kit replies + in-thread placeholder (original)

Steve's screenshot showed the existing Slack reply rendering as a giant unfurled `Agent-Native Dispatch` card stuck on every message, with no in-thread progress indicator and the deep-link inlined as plain text. This switches the Slack adapter to the Block Kit pattern Builder's existing slackbot uses (mirrors `/Users/steve/Projects/builder/ai-services/packages/service/integrations/slack/`).

**New flow:**

1. Webhook arrives → Slack adapter immediately posts a thread reply with a `Working on it…` context block (hourglass emoji, italic). Captures the message `ts` as a `placeholderRef` and bakes it into the queued task payload.
2. Processor finishes the agent loop → calls `chat.update` on the same `ts`, swapping the placeholder for a clean Block Kit response: a `section` block with the agent's mrkdwn answer, plus an `actions` block with an "Open thread" button URL-linking to the dispatch UI.
3. `unfurl_links` + `unfurl_media` are forced off so the deep-link no longer auto-unfurls into the giant card.

Adapters without `postProcessingPlaceholder` (Telegram, email) fall back to the existing post-on-completion behavior — no regression.

#### Interface changes

- `PlatformAdapter.postProcessingPlaceholder?(incoming) → { placeholderRef }` — optional, returns an opaque ref for in-place message updates.
- `PlatformAdapter.sendResponse(msg, ctx, opts?: { placeholderRef })` — adapters that support edits use the ref to update the placeholder; others ignore it and post fresh.
- `PlatformAdapter.formatAgentResponse(text, opts?: { threadDeepLinkUrl })` — the deep-link flows as structured data instead of inline `<url|text>` text, so adapters can render it as a button (Slack) or whatever else fits the platform (omit, inline as link, etc.).

#### App icon note

The bot's missing avatar is a separate concern — it has to be uploaded by the workspace admin at `api.slack.com/apps` → Basic Information → Display Information. The Slack API doesn't allow setting it programmatically. Added a step to the messaging-setup-panel onboarding list flagging this as recommended.

### 2. Fix Builder-connected chat on multi-tenant deploys (engine selection regression)

Reported by Brent on prod docs (Loom 2026-04-28): "It says it connected, but it doesn't seem to realize I'm connected once I do a chat."

**Root cause:** Commit 83a7e763 moved Builder credentials from `process.env.BUILDER_*` to per-user `app_secrets` rows (scope=user, scopeId=email). The OAuth callback writes there, and `/builder/status` reads from there — so the UI correctly shows "connected." But `resolveEngine` in `packages/core/src/agent/engine/registry.ts` only checks `process.env` and the global `settings` table; it never consulted `app_secrets`. On a multi-tenant deploy with no deploy-level `BUILDER_PRIVATE_KEY` env var, engine selection silently fell back to the default Anthropic engine (which had no API key either) and emitted `missing_api_key` → "Connect AI" gate re-appeared the moment the user tried to chat.

**Fix:** Added `detectEngineFromUserSecrets()` — async helper that mirrors `detectEngineFromEnv()` but reads from per-user `app_secrets`. Wired into `resolveEngine` ahead of the env-detect step, and into the `/_agent-native/agent-engine/status` endpoint so the engine-status UI gate stays consistent. Returns `null` for unauthenticated requests and for `local@localhost` so the existing dev-box / CLI / background-job paths are unchanged. Also handles the `AGENT_ENGINE_PREFER_BYO_KEY` escape hatch the same way `detectEngineFromEnv` does.

This also helps users who paste their own provider key (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) via the settings UI: previously chat only routed to the right engine when the deploy also had that var in `process.env`, now per-user app_secrets are sufficient.

#### Files

- `packages/core/src/agent/engine/registry.ts` — new `detectEngineFromUserSecrets()` + wired into `resolveEngine`
- `packages/core/src/server/core-routes-plugin.ts` — `/agent-engine/status` consults per-user secrets before falling back to env
- `packages/core/src/agent/engine/registry.spec.ts` — 4 new tests covering: null for unauthenticated / local-dev, picks Builder when user has Builder creds, `resolveEngine` end-to-end routes to Builder

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm prep` clean (494 tests pass — was 490 before, +4 for the new helper)
- [ ] After deploy: `@agent-native` in `#test-agent-native-slack-bot` →
  - thread shows "Working on it…" within a second
  - same message updates in place with `Open thread` button
  - no auto-unfurl card
- [ ] After deploy: on agent-native.com docs site, fresh user → connect Builder → send a chat message → response streams in (no "Connect AI" gate flash)

author: divyansh-db
body:
## Summary

Fixes the v1.114.0 regression reported in #5664 on the **`databricks_service_principal`** and **`databricks_service_principals`** data sources when used with an account-level provider. Both fail with:

> Error: cannot populate provider_config for service principal{s}: failed to resolve workspace_id: failed to get the workspace_id: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "": invalid syntax

### Root cause

PR #5492 (released in v1.114.0) added a post-Read hook in `common.Resource.ToResource()` that resolves and writes the effective `workspace_id` into `provider_config` for any resource with `provider_config` in its schema. The hook is skipped for *dual* resources at account level (`isDual && IsAccountLevel`), but neither SP data source was marked dual:

- `databricks_service_principal` had `provider_config` in its schema via `AddNamespaceInSchema` without `IsDual`
- `databricks_service_principals` used the legacy `common.DataResource` helper, which adds `provider_config` unconditionally and never sets `IsDual`

So at account level the post-Read hook ran, tried to resolve a workspace_id from a workspace client built on account-level config, and hit `strconv.ParseInt("", …)` because the SDK's workspace `/Me` call against an account host returns no `X-Databricks-Org-Id`.

SCIM is the rare API mounted on both workspace and account hosts, so the data source's Read itself succeeded against the account host — only then did the post-Read hook fail. That's why this regression manifested specifically on these two SCIM data sources and not on, say, `data_current_user` (which fails earlier when constructing a workspace client).

### Fix

Make both data sources properly dual — same pattern already used by `databricks_user`, `databricks_group`, and `databricks_current_config`:

- `common.AddApiField(s)` — adds the `api` field
- `IsDual: true` — `ToResource()` now skips the post-Read `provider_config` hook at account level
- `common.ValidateApiLevelForUnifiedHostFromData(d, m)` — fails the plan on a UnifiedHost when `api` is unset
- `DatabricksClientForDualResource(ctx, d)` — returns the original client at account level, no workspace routing
- `NewServicePrincipalsAPI(..., common.GetApiLevel(d))` — propagates the chosen api level so SCIM hits the right endpoint

For `data_service_principals` (plural) this also required converting from the legacy `common.DataResource` helper to a hand-written `common.Resource` so we can set `IsDual` and add the `api` field; the Read function now explicitly calls `DataToStructPointer` / `StructToData` / `SetId("_")` to match the previous `DataResource` semantics.

## Test plan

End-to-end verification on `azure-prod-acct` via deco — same cloud and provider type as the original report:

- [x] **Reproduced byte-for-byte** on unfixed code (`strconv.ParseInt: parsing "": invalid syntax` — exact match with issue):
  - `TestMwsAccDataSourceSPNByDisplayNameOnAccountNoApi` (singular) → FAIL
  - `TestMwsAccDataSourceSPNsByDisplayNameOnAccountNoApi` (plural) → FAIL
- [x] **All four new acceptance tests PASS on `azure-prod-acct`** with the fix:
  - `TestMwsAccDataSourceSPNByDisplayNameOnAccount` (singular, explicit `api = "account"`)
  - `TestMwsAccDataSourceSPNByDisplayNameOnAccountNoApi` (singular, host-based inference — exact configuration from the bug report)
  - `TestMwsAccDataSourceSPNsByDisplayNameOnAccount` (plural, explicit `api`)
  - `TestMwsAccDataSourceSPNsByDisplayNameOnAccountNoApi` (plural, host-based inference)
- [x] Also verified on `aws-prod-acct` for the singular variant (different inner failure — `Unable to load OAuth Config` — same wrapper, same fix)
- [x] Existing `TestDataServicePrincipal*` and `TestDataServicePrincipals*` unit tests still pass (workspace-level callers unaffected)
- [x] `NEXT_CHANGELOG.md` updated under Bug Fixes for both data sources

author: ph4ntom-rev
body:
This PR addresses a Directory Traversal vulnerability in the `antigravity_server.py` IDA plugin.

### 🎯 What
- Hardened the `/api/schema` endpoint against path manipulation and introduced schema caching.
- Fixed a critical Arbitrary File Read vulnerability in `import_c_header` by implementing path resolution and a security blocklist.

### ⚠️ Risk
Without this fix, an attacker could potentially read sensitive system files (like `/etc/passwd`) or internal IDA files if they can interact with the plugin's REST API.

### 🛡️ Solution
- Used `os.path.realpath` to resolve all user-provided or relative paths.
- Validated that the schema file being loaded is exactly `api_schema.json`.
- Implemented a blocklist for sensitive system directories (`/etc/`, `/proc/`, `C:\Windows\`, etc.) and blocked UNC path bypasses in `import_c_header`.
- Added `success: False` to error responses for better client-side error handling.

body:
## Summary

Move conversation history ownership from external callers into the core loop itself. This simplifies the `Agent.run()` contract and gives upper layers cleaner proxies for accessing session messages.

## Key Changes

### Core Loop
- **New `MessageList`** (`ouro/core/loop/message_list.py`): a dedicated mutable container for conversation history with `append/extend/replace_range/snapshot/clear`.
- **`Agent.run()` signature simplified**: removed `initial_messages` parameter; the loop constructs its own `MessageList` internally.
- **Hook protocol updated**: all callbacks now receive `MessageList` instead of `list[LLMMessage]`; added new `on_tool_results` callback.
- **Internal helpers refactored**: replaced generic `_chain_async` with typed helpers (`_build_outgoing`, `_chain_response`, `_chain_tool_call`, `_chain_tool_result`).

### Capabilities & Interfaces
- **`ComposedAgent` new proxy methods**: `get_session_messages()`, `get_session_message_count()`, `reset_memory()`, `rollback_incomplete_exchange()`, `compact_memory()`, `session_id` property. UI layers no longer reach into `memory.short_term` directly.
- **TUI/Bot adapted** to use the new `ComposedAgent` proxies.
- **New `/model` bot command**: supports `show` and `switch` subcommands for runtime model switching.
- **`VerificationHook` cleaned up**: simplified signatures, adapted to new message-passing contract.

### Tests
- Added `test_message_list.py` and `/model` command tests in `test_bot_server.py`.
- Updated `test_ralph_loop.py` and `test_reasoning_effort.py` for new signatures.

## RFC
- `rfc/016-loop-owned-message-list.md`

## Verification
- Full test suite: **627 passed, 1 skipped** ✅

body: ## Summary Extends the design-system text scale with three responsive headline tokens (`text-size-2xl`, `3xl`, `4xl`) so marketing pages can stop reaching for `text-[Npx]` arbitrary values for big headlines. Existing tokens unchanged. | Token | Mobile | md+ | | --- | --- | --- | | `text-size-xl` | 32px | 48px (existing, responsive) | | `text-size-2xl` | **40px** | **56px** | | `text-size-3xl` | **48px** | **64px** | | `text-size-4xl` | **56px** | **72px** | Mobile step ratios 32→40→48→56 = 1.25 / 1.20 / 1.17. md+ step ratios 48→56→64→72 = 1.17 / 1.14 / 1.13. Line heights tuned for display copy: 1.1 for 2xl/3xl, 1.05 for 4xl (vs 1.2 for the existing body/heading tokens). The scale-extension PR ships standalone (per the `@bluedot/db` schema-first convention). The follow-up PR migrating off-scale uses in `apps/website` onto these tokens lands separately, plus a third PR with an eslint rule blocking new arbitrary text-size values. ## Why Audit on `apps/website/src` showed **292 `text-[Npx]` arbitrary values vs 131 design-system `text-size-*` tokens** — 2.2× more arbitrary than tokens. PR #2362 just landed the mechanical 12/14/16/18/24px swaps (192 occurrences). The remaining ~100 are off-scale (15/13/28/20/36/40/etc.) — most are real headline sizes the existing 6-step scale couldn't express. The proposed values were reviewed via a local preview page (see screenshots below). ## Update — fix from review **Greptile flagged a scale inversion in the original commit**: `text-size-xl` is 48px at md+, but the original `text-size-2xl` was 40px there — so `xl` rendered larger than `2xl` on desktop. Force-pushed a fix that shifts 2xl and 3xl up so each new token is larger than `xl` at every breakpoint. | Was | Now | | --- | --- | | 2xl: 36→40px | 2xl: 40→56px | | 3xl: 48→56px | 3xl: 48→64px | | 4xl: 56→72px (unchanged) | 4xl: 56→72px | **Trade-off**: standalone 36px (×22) and 40px (×15) usages in the website no longer have an exact token match. PR 2b will resolve those case-by-case — either snap to `text-size-xl` (32→48 responsive), to `text-size-2xl` (40→56 responsive), or leave as `text-[36px]`/`text-[40px]` if the designer specifically wants a fixed-on-desktop size that isn't on the scale. ## Test plan - [x] `cd libraries/ui && npm test` — passes - [x] `cd libraries/ui && npm run lint` — passes - [x] `cd apps/website && npm run typecheck` — passes - [x] `cd apps/website && npm test` — passes (629/629, no snapshot deltas — no website code consumes the new tokens yet) - [x] Storybook renders the new sizes correctly (screenshots below — regenerated after the fix) ## Screenshots ### Storybook — design-system typography page Shows the full updated scale (`xxs` through `4xl`). Note that `4xl > 3xl > 2xl > xl > lg > md > sm > xs > xxs` at every breakpoint. | | Desktop | Mobile | | ---------- | --------------- | ------------------- | | `getting-started--docs` | | | ### Local preview page used for design review A throwaway preview page (on `dewi/text-scale-preview` branch — not in this PR) was used to visualise the proposed scale alongside real marketing components and snap-policy decisions. Captured here for context (note: shows the original 36/40 mobile values, not the revised 40/56). | | Desktop | Mobile | | ---------- | --------------- | ------------------- | | `/internal/text-scale-preview` | | | ## Files changed - `libraries/ui/src/default-config/tailwind.css` — three new `--text-size-{2xl,3xl,4xl}` definitions in `@theme`, the `:root` defaults, and the `md` breakpoint override. - `apps/storybook/src/GettingStarted.mdx` — Typography section updated to describe the new sizes; specimen list extended with rows for 4xl / 3xl / 2xl / xxs. ## Follow-ups - **PR 2b** (apps/website): migrate ~100 off-scale `text-[Npx]` values onto the new + existing tokens, with snap-to-nearest for ambiguous micro-typography (15/13/17/11/20/22/26/28/34px) and per-occurrence judgement for 36/40px headlines. - **PR 3** (eslint): add a rule blocking new `text-[\d+px]` in shared components. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

Wires the existing (but until now orphaned) AMS + adjust subsystem into
the live turn loop. Closes the last open item from the GC.1 plan
(post-turn AMS correction implementation).

- New \`memory/ams-registry.js\` — group-keyed AMS cache with id-only

  resumes with the same onDemand/recent membership it had on

- \`session.js\` — opens the registry alongside the SegmentIndex,
  passes it to Engine, persistAll()s on shutdown.

- \`engine.js\`:
  - \`#prepareAms\` per turn: resident from \`<scope>/summary.md\`
    (reusing the layer-A summaries already loaded), onDemand from
    preflow.entries, snapshot block appended to memory injection.
  - Cumulative input+output token usage tracked per query.
  - \`#runAdjustHook\` after end_turn drives \`runAdjust\` against the
    fastConfig adapter, persists the AMS when membership changes,
    tracks \`adjustRanThisSession\` per groupKey so the first turn
    always runs.

## Lifecycle

AMS is **group-level**, not per-turn or per-session. Files persist
across session deactivation. Resident layer is derived state and is
never persisted (rebuilt every turn from summary.md).

## Summary

### Journal behavior (Task 1A)
`_journal_add_chain` now branches on `save_intermediates`:
- **`True`** → existing per-step entries (each step has a real saved file).

  - Merge → `model_a → model_b` + `method @ alpha`

  pattern, `position: fixed; z-index: 200`). Body reuses the existing
  name / recipe / notes / image / delete form. Chain entries render their
  step list as a structured table inside the overlay. Dismiss via
  backdrop click, ✕ button, or Escape.

### Entry-tag surface removal (Task 2)
The `entry.type` badge replaces the `tags` array functionally. Removed:
- `tag=` query param + filter on `GET /studio/workshop/journal`

## Summary

First experiment-file migration. Single method:

| Method | Demonstrates |
|---|---|
| `measureBaseline` | 1000 samples × 10 representative instructions; `Punit.measuring(...)` typed entry point; factors = `LlmTuning.DEFAULT` |

### Pairing as a first-class concern

The migrated file's javadoc highlights what makes the empirical-pair pattern work: the same `ShoppingBasketUseCase.sampling(...)` + `LlmTuning.DEFAULT` that the measure uses is what `ShoppingBasketTest` also uses. The typed pipeline's inputs-identity (SHA-256 content hash) + factors-fingerprint integrity check guarantees the test won't silently consume a baseline measured under a different input set or configuration.

### What's not migrated, and why

The legacy file's second method (`measureBaselineWithGolden`) loaded inputs from a JSON fixture and used per-input expected values for instance-conformance checking via a `JsonMatcher`. **Not migrated** because it depends on:

1. Jackson being on the test-module classpath. The legacy framework arranged this via `@InputSource(file = ...)`; the typed pipeline asks authors to load fixtures themselves, and Jackson isn't a `testImplementation` in app-tests today.
2. The typed pipeline's matcher / `expectedOutputs` surface — wired in `Experiment.MeasureBuilder` but not yet exercised in the worked-example layer.

The fixture-loaded measure pattern (and the conformance-check semantic) lands when an upcoming worked example demonstrates `ValueMatcher` explicitly. The file's javadoc records the gap honestly rather than papering it over.

author: soleil-colza
body:
## Summary

Sixth and final content PR in the docs series. Adds the **Cookbook** nav group with six pages that show readers what TypeScript unlocks for an Arkor training run today, even at alpha.

The framing pivot from the original plan: instead of per-template walkthroughs (`triage` / `translate` / `redaction` each as a page), the Cookbook is now four extensibility recipes plus one customization page. The starter templates are still acknowledged, but as starting points to extend, not as ends in themselves. This matches the user request that the Cookbook should make it visible that "users can do various things by writing TS, even now".

## Pages

- `cookbook/overview.mdx` (new). Framing for the section + recipe index + the "callback exceptions are caught and retried" caveat that the recipes rely on.
- `cookbook/mid-run-eval.mdx` (new). Headline recipe: `onCheckpoint({ infer })` against a fixed prompt, runs at every checkpoint. The only path to mid-run inference today (Studio's Playground filters to completed jobs only).
- `cookbook/early-stopping.mdx` (new). `onLog` + `AbortController` + `trainer.cancel()`. Walks the two-step pattern explicitly so users do not assume `abortSignal` alone stops the backend job.
- `cookbook/notifications.mdx` (new). `onCompleted` / `onFailed` + a `fetch` to a Slack / Discord webhook. Stresses the inner try/catch so webhook outages do not retry through the SSE reconnect loop.
- `cookbook/programmatic-runs.mdx` (new). `runTrainer` for scripts; direct `start()` / `wait()` when you need full control. Concrete patterns for Next.js API routes, cron, CI smoke tests with `dryRun`, and multi-trainer orchestration.
- `cookbook/customizing-templates.mdx` (new). Four customization axes for the scaffolded `trainer.ts` (dataset, hyperparameters, callbacks, base model) and a composed example.

`docs/docs.json` gains a new **Cookbook** group with six pages, placed after SDK.

## Source-verified facts

All recipe code is checked against `packages/arkor/src/core/types.ts` and `packages/arkor/src/core/trainer.ts`:

- Callback signatures and the `Partial<TrainerCallbacks>` shape on `createTrainer`.
- `infer` returns the raw `Response`; the `stream: false` path lets the recipe stay short.
- `abortSignal` rejects `wait()`; `trainer.cancel()` is what stops the backend.
- Callback exceptions go through the SSE reconnect loop with `maxReconnectAttempts` defaulting to unlimited; recipes use outer state and inner `try/catch` to stay deterministic.
- `runTrainer` is the only public CLI-equivalent runner; `runBuild` / `runStart` / `runDev` are intentionally CLI-private.

The only forward-looking claim in the Cookbook is in `customizing-templates.mdx` where the base model paragraph notes that other models are on the roadmap. Everything else is feasible with the current public SDK.

## Conflict surface

- Touches `docs/cookbook/*` (new directory) and adds a new group to `docs/docs.json`. No overlap with PR #59 (CLI, eng-537), PR #60 (SDK, eng-538), or PR #61 (Studio, eng-539) on existing files.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @arkor/docs exec mint validate` passes.
- [x] No em dashes anywhere under `docs/cookbook/`.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @arkor/docs exec mint broken-links` flags references to `/sdk/*` because PR #60 has not merged into main yet. Those links are correct destinations; broken-links will be clean after the upstream SDK PR lands or this branch is rebased onto a main that already includes it.
- [ ] Mintlify preview deploy renders the six pages and the new Cookbook group in the nav.

body:
Modernizes the GitHub Actions workflows, makes them run on pull requests, and adds a release pipeline that automatically attaches a build artifact to GitHub Releases.

## Additions / Removals

- **Upgraded pinned actions** in `main.yaml` and `test.yaml`: `actions/checkout@v2` -> `@v6`, `actions/setup-node@v1` -> `@v6`, `actions/upload-artifact@master` -> `@v7`, `cypress-io/github-action@v2` -> `@v7`.
- **Single source of Node version**: replaced the hardcoded Node matrix with `node-version-file: 'package.json'`.
- Replaced the bespoke `actions/cache` step with the built-in `cache: 'npm'` on `setup-node`.
- Removed the `sudo apt-get install expect libnotify-bin` step - no longer needed with modern Cypress images.
- Test workflow now uploads Cypress screenshots and videos as artifacts on failure (7-day retention) for easier CI triage.
- **Run CI on pull requests**: both `main.yaml` and `test.yaml` now trigger on `pull_request` in addition to `push`. Previously these only ran on push, which meant a feature branch's failing build wouldn't block the PR being merged. With `pull_request` triggers, branch protection rules can now require green checks before merge.
- **New `release.yaml` workflow** triggered by pushing a `v*` tag. It validates the tag is semver and matches `package.json`'s `version`, runs `npm ci`, lint, and `build:static`, zips `dist/career-portal/browser` into `career-portal-v<version>.zip`, and creates a GitHub Release with auto-generated release notes and the zip attached. This addresses a recurring issue where release assets were missing from several recent releases - the build-and-attach step is now part of the tag workflow rather than a manual post-release action.
- Fixed `version.js` reading build metadata from `process.argv` instead of `process.env` - `Build#` and `Commit` were both always `UNKNOWN` before.
- Added nvm/fnm `engines` usage tips to `README.md`.

## Testing

- `test.yaml` and `main.yaml` run on PRs against the fork and pass.
- `release.yaml` triggered by pushing a `v*` tag produces a GitHub Release with the static zip attached.
https://github.com/ChrisLane/career-portal/releases/tag/v3.7.1

## Screenshots


## Notes

- The [advanced install docs](https://bullhorn.github.io/career-portal/advanced-install.html) document a `career-portal-v<version>-dynamic.zip` asset (the SSR / dynamic build) alongside the static zip. This asset has not been published on any recent release and is **not** addressed by this PR - the new release workflow only produces the static zip (`career-portal-v<version>.zip`). Adding the dynamic build output to the release workflow should be tracked as a separate piece of work so it can be scoped and reviewed on its own.

* [x] Code can be automatically merged (no conflicts)

author: kilo-code-bot[bot]
body:
## Summary

Upgrades `actions/download-artifact` `v4` → `v8` everywhere in `publish.yml`, and switches the `kilo-cli` upload to `actions/upload-artifact@v7` with `archive: false`.

## Why

Run [25101862100](https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/actions/runs/25101862100) silently failed because `download-artifact@v4.3.0` only **logs a warning** when the downloaded artifact's digest doesn't match what the server advertised. The `build-vscode` job happily proceeded with a corrupt/incomplete `packages/opencode/dist/` and then failed 36 minutes later at "CLI binary not found" — a symptom far removed from the real cause. This made the flake hard to diagnose and easy to misattribute to the build script.

`download-artifact@v8` defaults `digest-mismatch: error`, so the same corruption now fails the **download** step itself with a clear message. That's the main win of this PR: a class of silent failure becomes a loud, scoped failure.

Paired with that, `upload-artifact@v7`'s `archive: false` removes the redundant zip-wrapper that currently gets stored around our already-zstd'd tarball. The tarball now travels as-is; `download-artifact@v8` auto-detects via `Content-Type` and `skip-decompress: true` makes the intent explicit.

## What's NOT fixed by this

The underlying 2–3 GB artifact-service limits are not addressed here; those need artifact-size reduction (split by platform, drop the `.tar.gz`/`.zip` release archives that `build.ts` writes back into `dist/`, etc.). This PR only changes how the artifact is transported.

## Caveats

With `archive: false`, upload-artifact's `name:` input is ignored and the artifact is named after the file (`kilo-cli.tar.zst`). The two consumers (`build-vscode`, `publish`) have been updated to use `name: kilo-cli.tar.zst`.

The `kilo-vscode` upload stays on `v4` because it uploads a directory of `.vsix` files, and `archive: false` requires the glob to resolve to a single file.

---

author: mycognosist
body:
We previously observed flakiness in the `leave_overlay_on_drop` gossip test, whose purpose is to ensure cleanup of state when gossip stream handles - or the entire gossip system - are dropped. The test would simply hang without completion.

I tracked the behaviour down to a failure to join the gossip overlay after the p2panda `Gossip` object had been dropped and recreated from scratch for one of the two nodes in the test. This suggested that the node which remained running may have held some incorrect connection state relating to the downed node; the assumption being that this prevented the latest overlay connection attempt to fail.

On further inspection, I realised that the call to gracefully shut down iroh gossip (from within the `post_stop` method of the gossip manager actor) was not being executed. Calling `gossip.shutdown()` directly in `post_stop`, without spawning it in a tokio task, resulted in the shut down but caused a panic of unknown origin. My suspicion is that one of the other gossip actors was causing the panic.

The implemented solution is three-fold (all in the `Drop` impl for p2panda):

1) Drain all children of the gossip manager actor
2) Send the newly-added Shutdown message to the gossip manager actor
3) Drain the gossip manager actor

The test now passes reliably without any panics.

body:
## Summary

PR 4 of the channel-package extraction series. **Stacked on #411** — review #405 → #408 → #411 first, then this PR shows only the type hoist.

Moves the five most heavily referenced pure-data types into \`cmd/wuphf/channelui/types.go\`:

- \`BrokerReaction\`
- \`BrokerMessageUsage\`
- \`BrokerMessage\`
- \`RenderedLine\`
- \`ThreadedMessage\`

These shapes flow through every renderer, broker cmd-builder, and test in the channel cluster. Hoisting them now unblocks the actual renderer move (next PR) without churning every callsite.

## Why aliases instead of renaming everything

\`cmd/wuphf/channelui_aliases.go\` adds:

\`\`\`go
type (
    brokerReaction     = channelui.BrokerReaction
    brokerMessageUsage = channelui.BrokerMessageUsage
    brokerMessage      = channelui.BrokerMessage
    renderedLine       = channelui.RenderedLine
    threadedMessage    = channelui.ThreadedMessage
)
\`\`\`

Type aliases share field access and method semantics with the underlying type, so every existing usage like \`brokerMessage{ID: ...}\`, \`msg.From\`, \`func(msgs []brokerMessage) ...\` continues to compile unchanged. This is the bridge mechanism the plan calls for: keep the channel cluster compiling at HEAD while the actual code physically migrates over several PRs.

The aliases are temporary. PR 9 (final cleanup) drops them once nothing references the lowercase names anymore.

## What changed

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| \`cmd/wuphf/channelui/types.go\` (new) | +63 |
| \`cmd/wuphf/channelui_aliases.go\` (new) | +18 |
| \`cmd/wuphf/channel.go\` (deletes) | −38 |
| \`cmd/wuphf/channel_render.go\` (deletes) | −9 |

Net: 4 files, 81 insertions, 47 deletions.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bash scripts/test-go.sh\` — all 34 packages green
- [x] \`go vet ./...\` — clean
- [x] \`golangci-lint run ./...\` — 0 issues
- [x] \`go build ./cmd/wuphf\` — binary builds
- [ ] CI passes on draft PR

## Why so small

The original plan called for moving the actual renderer files in this PR (\`channel_render.go\`, \`channel_mailboxes.go\`, \`channel_thread.go\`, etc., ~3500 LoC). Splitting that into "types first, files next" gives reviewers a tractable diff and lets the next PR be a near-mechanical file move now that the type contract is stable in channelui.

## Next in stack

- PR 4b: Move \`channel_messages.go\`, \`channel_mailboxes.go\`, \`channel_thread.go\`, \`channel_layout.go\`, \`channel_composer.go\`, \`channel_window.go\`, \`channel_needs_you.go\` into channelui (small/medium leaves first)
- PR 4c: Move \`channel_render.go\` (1407 lines, split into render_office/render_calendar/render_policy/etc.)
- PR 5+: Workspace cluster, sidebar/splash, broker integrations, the model itself, cleanup

## Summary

- The `scan` step in `.agents/pipelines/ops-issue-quality.yaml` declared its `quality-report.json` output under `.agents/artifacts/`, which is the framework's INTERNAL injection target (populated by `memory.inject_artifacts`), not where pipelines should write outputs.
- Wave convention is `.agents/output/<name>.<ext>` for declared pipeline output artifacts. Using the wrong path breaks downstream consumers and violates the documented convention.
- Updated both `output_artifacts[0].path` and the matching `handover.contract.source` to `.agents/output/quality-report.json`. The artifact name (`quality-report`) is unchanged, so the `enhance` step's `inject_artifacts` reference (which is name-based, not path-based) continues to resolve correctly.

## Audit context

Prior audit flagged this as a path inconsistency that breaks downstream consumers and violates the `.agents/output/` convention for declared pipeline outputs.

## Note on `enhance` step `{{ input }}`

The audit also flagged the `enhance` step prompt referencing `{{ input }}` without a corresponding `memory.input` block. Verified this is a **false positive**: the pipeline declares a top-level `input:` block (lines 19-25) with `source: cli, type: string`, so `{{ input }}` is auto-resolved by Wave's templating from the pipeline-level input. No fix needed.

The `enhance` step's other output (`enhancement-summary.md`) also lives under `.agents/artifacts/` but was NOT flagged by the audit and is left untouched in this PR to keep scope tight. If the same convention should apply, it can be addressed in a follow-up.

## What are the changes about?

## Problem
When crediting an invoice in Creditors → Orders, the quantity field on 
the credit note order lines is empty/zero instead of mirroring the original.

Reproduced on test_7 (Rotary). Works correctly on test_12 (Havemøbelland).

## Root Cause
The original code discarded the invoice quantity entirely and tried to 
rebuild it from the `batch_kob` goods receipt table. In test_7, that 
table had no matching rows for the invoiced items, so quantity stayed 0.

## Fix
- Read `antal` directly from `ordrelinjer` (the invoice line itself) 
  before any reset — this is the ground truth
- Save it as `$original_antal` before the batch logic runs
- Fall back to `original_antal * -1` when `batch_kob` returns no rows

- Preserves existing behaviour for environments where batch_kob is populated

author: kim-em
body:
## Summary

A parametric `run` whose every rung was filtered out by the warmup-trim or signal-floor filter still exited 0, masking a calibration bug behind a benign `verdict: inconclusive (cMin=—, cMax=—, β=—)` report. This PR adds a dedicated exit code (`2`) so scripts and CI can fail loudly without parsing stdout. Closes #47.

- New `BenchmarkResult.noUsableData : Bool := r.ratios.isEmpty && !r.budgetTruncated` and `exitNoUsableData : UInt32 := 2` in `LeanBench/Core.lean`. `ratios` is the canonical filtered set produced by `Stats.ratiosFromPoints` (already drops non-`ok`, doubling-probe, below-floor, and `param < 2` rows), so "zero verdict-eligible rows" is exactly `ratios.isEmpty`.
- `runRunCmd` (via `handleBaselineAndExport`) and `runCompareCmd` return `exitNoUsableData` when any parametric result is in this state, and emit a one-line stderr summary listing the offending benchmarks. This supersedes the baseline-regression code `1` — if the harness has no data, the regression check itself was meaningless.
- Budget-truncated runs (`--total-seconds`) are excluded: those are user-requested early stops, surfaced by the budget summary instead — not calibration bugs.
- New `LeanBenchTestNoUsableData.lean` test exe wired into `lakefile.toml` and the CI workflow. Pure unit tests on the predicate (incl. the budget-truncated and all-errored edge cases), plus integration tests using a `signalFloorMultiplier := 1.0e9` benchmark to force every row below floor and assert `Cli.dispatch ["run", NAME]` returns `2`. A negative control with the floor disabled still returns `0`. `compare` propagates the same code.
- Quickstart docs gain an exit-code table.

I asked Codex for a second opinion on the predicate choice (`ratios.isEmpty` vs. an advisory-based check); it agreed `ratios` is the better source of truth (advisories are presentation-oriented; `ratios` is the actual verdict input) and that the `2`-beats-`1` precedence is coherent.

## Test plan

- [x] `lake build` — all 120 targets build clean
- [x] `no_usable_data_benchmark_test` — new test exe passes (predicate unit tests + run/compare integration with both below-floor and clean negative-control cases)
- [x] `budget_benchmark_test` — still passes after the budget-truncated exclusion
- [x] `cli_errors_benchmark_test`, `e2e_benchmark_test`, `format_benchmark_test`, `export_benchmark_test`, `advisory_benchmark_test` — all unchanged behavior

author: pacphi
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the v4 component source modes plan (ADR-028 / DDD-08):

- **`OciSource`** — real impl wrapping the existing `RegistryClient` (oci-client + cosign + cache). Captures the manifest digest at fetch time and records it in the lockfile descriptor so re-resolutions of the same tag are byte-stable. `supports_strict_oci()` flips on after a successful cosign pipeline run.
- **`LocalOciSource`** — reads OCI image-layout v1.1 directories. Walks `index.json`, locates the registry-core artifact by media type or `org.sindri.registry.kind=registry-core` annotation, parses the embedded `index.yaml`. Optional `artifact_ref` lets callers pin a specific manifest digest.
- **`--strict-oci` admission gate** — fails the resolve when any component is served by a non-production-grade source (anything other than `Oci` or `LocalOci`). Layered after Gates 1–4 so it sees the final source mix and reports every offender at once. Non-strict mode emits exactly one `tracing::warn!` summarising the source mix.

## What's in scope

- `v4/crates/sindri-registry/src/source/oci.rs` — `OciSource` + `OciSourceConfig`
- `v4/crates/sindri-registry/src/source/local_oci.rs` — `LocalOciSource` + `LocalOciSourceConfig` + deterministic test-fixture generator (no binary blobs committed)
- `v4/crates/sindri-resolver/src/lib.rs` — `apply_strict_oci_gate` + `ResolveOptions::strict_oci`
- `v4/crates/sindri-resolver/src/error.rs` — new `ResolverError::SourceNotProductionGrade { offenders }`
- `v4/crates/sindri/src/commands/resolve.rs` + `main.rs` — `--strict-oci` flag + sindri.yaml `registry.policy.strict_oci` precedence
- `v4/crates/sindri-core/src/manifest.rs` — `RegistrySection { policy: Option<RegistryPolicy { strict_oci }> }`
- `v4/schemas/bom.json` + `v4/schemas/registry-source.json` — regenerated
- `v4/docs/SOURCES.md` — Phase status table updated

## What's NOT in scope

- **Phase 3** (`GitSource`, `sindri registry serve`, `sindri registry prefetch`) — explicitly deferred per the plan.
- **Phase 4** (sindri.yaml `registry.sources:` schema migration, `--explain` source attribution, CI templates, MIGRATION_FROM_V3 entries).
- The full per-source OCI client tests against live registries — kept behind the existing `live-oci-tests` feature flag, untouched.

## Notable decisions

- **Phase 2.1 + 2.2 shipped as a single commit** rather than two — `RegistrySource::LocalOci` carries a typed `LocalOciSourceConfig`, and splitting the commits would leave the enum in a half-defined state for one commit. The PR has three logical commits: 2.1+2.2 (sources), 2.3 (gate), and the existing v4 tip.
- **Sync trait, async client.** The `Source` trait is sync to keep the resolver pipeline simple. `OciSource::fetch_index` bridges to the async `RegistryClient` via `block_on_async`, which detects an active tokio runtime and hops to a worker thread to avoid the "runtime within a runtime" panic. Sync callers get a cheap current-thread runtime.
- **Strict-OCI report style.** A single `tracing::warn!` per resolve listing all offenders, not per-component. Keeps CI logs scannable without losing actionable detail.
- **Flag precedence.** `--strict-oci` OR `registry.policy.strict_oci` — i.e., the flag forces-on, the config never forces-off the flag. Documented on both surfaces.
- **Descriptor parity.** `LocalOciSource` and `OciSource` produce byte-identical `manifest_digest` values for the same artifact (regression test `descriptor_round_trips_between_oci_and_local_oci`).

## New dependencies

- `oci-spec = "0.7"` (Apache-2.0) — workspace-level dep added for image-layout v1.1 spec types. Carried for forward compatibility; the actual implementation reads `index.json` via `serde_json` so the surface area is small. No new RustSec advisories at time of write.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd v4 && cargo build --workspace` clean
- [x] `cd v4 && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cd v4 && cargo fmt --all --check` clean
- [x] `cd v4 && cargo test --workspace` — 621 passing (was 593; +28)
- [x] `cd v4 && cargo run -p schema-gen -- --check` clean
- [x] Acceptance #1: `--strict-oci` rejects a `LocalPath` lockfile (`strict_oci_admission::strict_oci_rejects_lockfile_with_local_path_source`)
- [x] Acceptance #2: `--strict-oci` accepts an Oci-only lockfile (`strict_oci_admission::strict_oci_accepts_lockfile_with_only_oci_sources`)
- [x] Acceptance #3: `LocalOciSource` and `OciSource` emit identical manifest digests for the same artifact (`local_oci_fixture::descriptor_round_trips_between_oci_and_local_oci`)

## References

- [ADR-028 — Component source modes for development and air-gap](v4/docs/ADRs/028-component-source-modes.md)
- [DDD-08 — Registry Source Domain](v4/docs/DDDs/08-registry-source-domain.md)
- [Plan §2 — `OciSource` and `LocalOciSource`](v4/docs/plan/source-modes-implementation.md)

author: danielelerede-oet
body:
## Add configurable custom industry demand allocation modes

This PR introduces a configurable framework to control how additional
custom industry demand (e.g. ammonia and methanol) is allocated across
the network.

Custom industry demand is now decomposed into:

-   **Baseline demand**: derived from plant-level CSV data (always treated as grey production)
-   **Growth demand**: the difference between target demand and baseline, handled according to the selected allocation mode

The share of e-fuels (`e_share`) is applied **only to the growth
component**, while baseline demand remains unchanged.

## New configuration options

``` yaml
custom_industry:
    mode: brownfield_optimised_growth # choose from ["proportional_existing_capacity" or  brownfield_optimised_growth" or "greenfield_optimised_growth"]
```

## Implemented allocation modes

### 1. Proportional allocation

All demand is distributed proportionally to existing plant capacities.

### 2. Brownfield optimised growth

Growth is optimised only across existing nodes.

### 3. Greenfield optimised growth

Growth is optimised across all feasible nodes.

## Current Limitations

-   No transport costs
-   No transport constraints
-   Possible spatial concentration
