author: 1vav
body:
## Summary

- **`validateName` regex was too strict** — the `[\w.\- ]` allowlist rejected valid Unicode characters (em-dashes `–`, accented letters, etc.) that are perfectly legal in filenames. This caused `safeName` to return `null`, `/api/resolve` to return 400, and the client to fall back to opening the target as a diagram.
- **Wikilink basename matching was missing** — the `notes`/`diagrams` arrays store full relative paths (e.g. `subfolder/My Note`) but wikilinks are basename-only (`[[My Note]]`). Exact-path matching failed for any file not in the workspace root, hitting the same diagram fallback.

## Changes

- `src/workspace.js` — replace allowlist regex with a blocklist that only rejects filesystem-unsafe chars (`/ \ : * ? " < > |` and control chars); all printable Unicode is now valid
- `src/viewer/entry.jsx` — `openFile` now tries basename matching (`n.split("/").pop()`) in addition to full-path matching
- `src/viewer-server.js` — `/api/resolve` glob fallback now also compares by basename
- `vendor/` — rebuilt at v1.2.0

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a note whose name contains an em-dash via a wikilink — should open as a note, not show "doesn't look like a diagram"
- [ ] Open a note that lives in a subdirectory via `[[basename-only]]` wikilink — resolves correctly
- [ ] Path traversal (`../secret`), absolute paths, and null bytes are still rejected by `validateName`

但仅凭你发的这段 PDF 原始内容，我**无法判断你们“已经做了什么”**（那需要看你们仓库里的代码/README/演示视频脚本等）。我先把“按 guideline 推断的必做/加分项清单”给你们列出来，你们对照勾选；然后你把仓库里现状补充给我，我再给出“你们已经完成 vs 还差什么”的精确结论和冲刺计划。

---

## 1) 你们现在能确定“已经做了什么”
从你这句话里能确定的只有：

- 你们**选择了 chatbot 方向**
- 你们准备**冲满 bonus**
- 项目必须包含 **GUI（图形界面）**（这是 compulsory）

除此之外（比如是否已经做了 GUI、是否接了本地/在线 LLM、是否有 history、是否有网络对战等），目前信息不够，不能断言。

---

## 2) Chatbot 方向（必做项）一般需要做到什么（按 guideline 的意图）
### A. Compulsory：GUI（50%那部分的核心）
你们的 chatbot 项目需要至少包含：
- 一个可运行的 GUI（通常是 Tkinter / PyQt / CustomTkinter）
- GUI 里能完成基本交互：输入框、发送按钮、消息显示区（滚动/分页更好）
- 程序结构清晰（通常会要求“多文件组织/类/函数拆分”，PDF 里也有“Importing classes/functions from another .py file”的专门章节）

### B. Chatbot 子方向通常还隐含这些最低要求（为了像“完整项目”而不是 demo）
- 有基本的对话流程（不是只 print）
- 有一定的状态管理（至少能保存当前会话消息）
- 有异常处理（网络/模型不可用时 UI 不崩）
- 有清晰的运行说明（README：怎么装依赖、怎么运行）

---

## 3) 想拿满所有 bonus：你们需要把“Selective topic(s)+Bonus”也做满

- **4.2 Selective Topic(s) (20%) + Bonus (up to 35%)**

author: bluefa
body:
## Summary

- Add `/codex-simplify` — a Codex CLI counterpart of `/simplify`. Mirrors `/simplify`'s `Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3` flow but runs the three review lenses (Reuse / Quality / Efficiency) as **parallel Codex CLI calls** (`gpt-5.5` / `xhigh`) instead of parallel Claude sub-agents. Codex reviews; Claude owns Phase 3 (apply the fixes).
- Sync to Claude `/simplify`: the lens checklists are kept **verbatim from /simplify** (Reuse 3 items, Quality 8 items, Efficiency 7 items) so a Codex pass and a Claude pass produce comparable findings. Phase 1 / Phase 3 wording also follows `/simplify` directly.
- Engine concerns (full-access flag, pinned model, fresh-base fetch, foreground bash + 600s timeout, no-auto-apply) are pulled from `/codex-review` via cross-references rather than restated, so the two skills stay in lockstep.

## Why a separate skill (and not just an arg on `/codex-review`)

`/codex-review` is a single-call sign-off that produces one verdict. `/codex-simplify` is the cleanup loop: three lens-specific reviews fan out in parallel, findings are aggregated, and Claude applies the fixes — the same shape as `/simplify`. Splitting them keeps each skill's instructions tight.

## Self-review

Ran `/simplify`'s 3-agent pattern on this branch (Reuse / Quality / Efficiency) before opening the PR. Applied:
- Trimmed verbatim duplication of `/codex-review`'s execution principles, command template, failure handling, prohibitions — kept core inline, pointed to `/codex-review` for rationale.
- Removed the speculative `git diff HEAD~1` empty-fallback (and the contradiction it created with the "if no changes, stop" rule); aligned default scope with `/simplify` exactly (`git diff`, or `git diff HEAD` if staged).
- Extracted a single **wrapper prompt** for STEP 1 / STEP 3 / Constraints — each lens prompt now provides only its STEP 2 checklist, eliminating ~45 lines of triplication and the drift risk it created.
- Frontmatter description now says "Codex reviews, Claude applies the fixes" so skill discovery surfaces the Phase 3 split.
- Dropped a redundant `Run each call as foreground Bash` line (already covered in execution principle 4) and a redundant pre-search bullet inside Lens 1 STEP 1.

## Test plan

- [ ] `/codex-simplify` (no args) on a working tree with diff — three Codex calls fan out in parallel, three lens outputs surface verbatim, Claude applies findings in Phase 3.
- [ ] `/codex-simplify uncommitted` on a tree with untracked files — Codex receives `cat`-ed contents of untracked files in addition to `git diff HEAD`.
- [ ] `/codex-simplify commit <sha>` — single commit reviewed.
- [ ] `/codex-simplify base=main` — three-dot diff against `main` reviewed.
- [ ] One lens times out → other two continue; failure handling matches `/codex-review`.

author: samireltabal
body:
## Summary

Builds the behavioral core of the Personal CRM on top of PR #17's schema. Backend only — UI lands in the next PR.

**Stacked on PR #17** (base = `feat/personal-crm`). Once #17 merges to main, I'll rebase this onto main so the diff narrows to just Phase B–D.

## What's new

### Phase B — service layer
- **`EmailAddress`** value object — RFC-5322 mailbox parsing, transactional-sender detection (`config/people.php` regex + domain blocklist), fallback display name from local part
- **`PersonResolver`** — find-or-create from email with normalization + default-context attribution. Never materializes Person rows for `noreply@*`, `do-not-reply@*`, mailgun.org and friends
- **`InteractionRecorder`** — bumps `person.last_contact_at` via `max(current, occurred_at)` so back-dated manual notes never reverse the timeline; dedups via `unique(user_id, channel, external_id)`; dispatches `SummarizeInteractionJob` unless caller pre-supplied a summary or the feature is disabled
- **`ContactStaleness`** — query helper for "haven't talked to in N days"
- **`SummarizeInteractionJob`** + **`InteractionSummaryAgent`** — queued one-sentence factual summary, configurable provider/model via `PEOPLE_SUMMARIZE_*`; on any failure falls back to a 280-char truncation so the timeline UI is never blank

### Phase C — auto-population hooks
- **`InboundEmailController`** — after the existing classifier runs, calls `PersonResolver`+`InteractionRecorder`, wrapped in try/catch so a CRM failure can't break the inbound-email pipeline. Uses `message_id` for cross-forward dedup.
- **`GmailTool::draftReply`** — when the LLM drafts a reply, records an outbound email interaction tagged `metadata.draft=true`. Real send capture lands when actual Gmail send is added.

### Phase D — REST API + AI tools
| | |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/people` | list with `q`, `tag`, `stale=1`, `sort` |
| `POST /api/v1/people` | create + optional `emails[]`/`phones[]` |
| `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/people/{id}` | show/update/soft-delete |
| `GET/POST /api/v1/people/{id}/interactions` | timeline + manual log |

Search uses `LOWER(col) LIKE` driven by the trgm indexes from #17 on Postgres; falls back to portable `LOWER+LIKE` on SQLite for tests.

Seven new AI tools auto-discovered by `ToolRegistry`:
- `find_person` · `list_people` · `create_person` · `update_person` · `log_interaction` · `recent_interactions` · `find_stale_contacts`

`create_person` and `log_interaction` honor the existing `MAX_RECORDS_PER_TURN = 3` guardrail.

## Tests

| Phase | New | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|
| B (services) | 33 | — |
| C (auto-population) | 6 | — |
| D (API + tools) | 23 | — |
| **Total this PR** | **62** | — |
| Suite | — | **405 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail** |

## Test plan

- [x] `php artisan test --compact` — all green
- [x] Pint clean
- [ ] Smoke: forward an email to your inbound address → check `/api/v1/people`
- [ ] Smoke: ask in chat "find Sara" → `find_person` tool fires and returns hit
- [ ] Smoke: ask in chat "who haven't I talked to in 90 days" → `find_stale_contacts` fires
- [ ] Smoke: GmailTool draft reply → check the recipient appears as a Person with an outbound interaction tagged `metadata.draft`

## Caveats / scope choices

- **Telegram/WhatsApp auto-population dropped from Phase C** — those channels are user-↔-bot, not third-party contacts. Surfaced this in conversation; dropping it removed two hooks but matches the actual data semantics.
- **Gmail "send" capture is draft-only for now** — `GmailTool` only drafts replies, no real send. Capture metadata flags `draft=true` so this becomes a 5-line upgrade when real send lands.
- **No Livewire UI yet** — that's the next PR.
- **No birthday reminders yet** — also next PR.

## Open follow-ups (next PR)

- `/people` list + `/people/{id}` detail Livewire UI
- `people:birthday-check` daily scheduled command
- Dashboard "stale contacts" widget
- Sidebar nav link
- README + memory updates

author: hermeticormus
body:
## Why

`cosmic-term` has no equivalent of `xterm -geometry` or `alacritty --dimensions` — users triggering terminals from keyboard shortcuts or scripts can't pre-size the window, and UI resizes don't persist across launches. This is the ask in #771.

## What changed

`src/main.rs` gains a `--window-size <WxH>` flag (e.g. `--window-size 1280x720`), parsed from `clap_lex` alongside the existing `--working-directory` and `--no-daemon` handling.

When set, the value threads through libcosmic's `Settings::size(iced::Size::new(width, height))` before `cosmic::app::run`, so it takes effect on first paint. When unset, behavior is unchanged (libcosmic default of 1024x768).

Both lower- and uppercase separator (`x` / `X`) accepted. Floating-point dimensions accepted. Invalid input (missing separator, non-numeric, zero, negative) exits with a one-line error.

## How to test

```
cargo build --bin cosmic-term
./target/debug/cosmic-term --window-size 1280x720    # opens at the requested size
./target/debug/cosmic-term --window-size foo         # → "Invalid argument for --window-size: expected WxH, got \"foo\"", exit 1
./target/debug/cosmic-term --window-size             # → "Missing argument for --window-size", exit 1
./target/debug/cosmic-term --help                    # documents the new flag
cargo test --bin cosmic-term tests::                 # 6 new unit tests for parse_window_size
```

## Notes

- Naming follows the issue ("window-size") and the existing flag style. `--geometry` was considered but `xterm`'s geometry syntax (`WxH+X+Y`) implies position support, which would need a separate libcosmic API; staying with `--window-size` keeps the scope honest.
- Logical pixels (matching libcosmic's `iced::Size`), so the flag composes correctly with `COSMIC_SCALE`.
- 6 unit tests cover the parser: lower/uppercase separator, floats, missing separator, non-numeric, zero/negative.

Closes #771.

body:
#### 8f7132dd0edc7900ce7a7d3c9614cb30229bb72d 
[JSC] Make `GatherAvailableAncestors` O(N) instead of O(N^2)
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=313753

Reviewed by Yusuke Suzuki.

The spec's "execList does not contain m" check [1] was implemented with
Vector::contains, making each gather call O(N^2) over a sync-parent
cascade. Replace it with "m.[[PendingAsyncDependencies]] != 0", which
is equivalent within a single gather call (spec step 1.a.iv guarantees
one direction; the other follows from pending only being driven to 0
inside step 1.a.v + 1.a.vi.1, with no concurrent mutation). V8 DCHECKs
the same invariant [2].

Both directions are verified by ASSERT.

author: yashnevatia
body:
Fixed by adjusting limit
```
L3: Already processed transactions could be re-processed

File: chain_capabilities\aptos\actions\tx_info_retriever.go

In the for loop of paginateBackwards, pageSize items will be processed even if the actual number of the remaining items of the last iteration is less than pageSize. This case could be optimized, ensuring that only new TXs are processed. Otherwise, processed transactions could be reprocessed only consuming resources.


```

Fixed by fixing pagesize
```
L4: The derived pagination window could degrade the backwards lookup with many small RPC calls

File: chain_capabilities\aptos\actions\tx_info_retriever.go

GetSuccessfulTransmissionInfo and GetFailedTransmissionInfo derive the backward-pagination pageSize directly from the size of the initial withQuickRetry result. If that first call returns an unusually small page, phase 2 can degrade into many small RPC calls to cover the search window. A possible solution would be to define a bare minimum pageSize instead of always using len(txns) as-is.
```

author: hsyl20
body:
When a preprocessed file does @#include "rel/path.h"@, C99 §6.10.2 requires the implementation to look first in a path that depends on the source of the directive — gcc/clang look in the directory of the file containing the @#include@. HPP was deliberately /not/ updating the @dir@ field on entry to a nested include (per the comment that warned against using the config lens), so quoted includes were always resolved relative to the original input file's directory plus the system include path.

This breaks any header that uses a sibling include from a subdirectory of the search path: the sibling lookup needs the includer's directory, which HPP never had.

Switch 'streamNewFile' to update both @curFileName@ and the @dir@ field when entering an included file, and restore both on exit.

A new test case in tests/AsLib.hs (with fixtures under tests/include-data) exercises the file-resolution path that 'expand' previously skipped: it cd's into the fixture root and preprocesses an initial @#include "sub/outer.h"@, where outer.h itself does @#include "inner.h"@ — only resolvable through the includer's own directory.

author: bidalufias
body:
## Summary

Live testing on Normal felt too fast too quickly. Three balance changes:

- **Halfway-gate spawn rule**: a new item only appears once every existing waste item has cleared the **upper half** of the playfield. Stops items bunching at the top and gives the player time to read each fresh emoji before the next one shows up, even on Rush. The gate combines with (not replaces) the per-level spawn interval and the concurrent-item cap.
- **Round shortened to 5 sorts** (was 10). Smaller, more frequent steps rather than a big jump every 10.
- **Gentler 6-level ramp**: smaller per-level deltas so the faster cadence doesn't feel punishing. Top speed `2.4 → 2.3`, top cap `5 → 4`. Pool sizes still reach all 35 items at level 6.

```
L1: 1.0 / 2200ms / cap 1 / 5 types
L2: 1.2 / 1900ms / cap 2 / 10
L3: 1.4 / 1600ms / cap 2 / 18
L4: 1.7 / 1400ms / cap 3 / 25
L5: 2.0 / 1200ms / cap 3 / 30
L6: 2.3 / 1000ms / cap 4 / 35
```

## Test plan

- [ ] On Normal, two items never spawn back-to-back without the previous one passing the playfield's vertical midpoint.
- [ ] Level bumps every 5 sorts, capped at 6.
- [ ] Final level (6) tops out at 4 simultaneous items, never 5.
- [ ] Chill / Rush presets continue to scale spawn interval and fall speed proportionally.

body:
## Summary

Closes [P1a-1 in `docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md). Lays the analyzer foundation for Phase 1a — `normalize(input)` is the input to every later analyzer ticket (P1a-2 keyword DB, P1a-3 detection priority chain, P1a-4 confidence, P1a-5 grouping).

Implements the design at [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-30-p1a-1-entity-normalization-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-30-p1a-1-entity-normalization-design.md).

- **`normalize(input)`** — pure function in `@lovelacer/analyzer` that converts HA's `HaEntityRegistryEntry[]` + `HaDeviceRegistryEntry[]` into `NormalizedEntity[]`. Entity passthrough fields, friendly-name resolution priority (`name → original_name → humanize(objectId)`), device attachment via `Map<id, HaDeviceRegistryEntry>` lookup, malformed entity_id throws (covers no dot / leading dot / trailing dot / empty).
- **No area inheritance.** `entity.haAreaId` stays the entity's own `area_id` only — device-area inheritance is the detection chain's job per [HEURISTICS.md](docs/HEURISTICS.md). An anti-regression test pins this.
- **`humanize(slug)`** — private helper, title-cases each underscore-separated word with no acronym preservation. `aqara_th_158d` → `Aqara Th 158d`.
- **`fixtureToHaRegistries(fixture)`** — bridge helper at `tests/fixtures/_builder/to-ha-registries.ts` that converts P0-2's `Fixture` shape to HA wire shape. Reusable for P1a-2/3 integration tests.
- **Integration test** — runs `normalize` against the canonical 159-entity `english-cluttered` fixture and asserts signal counts (disabled / hidden / diagnostic) round-trip.

Tooling: local `packages/analyzer/vitest.config.ts` so analyzer tests are discoverable (the orphan-test pattern flagged in P0-2's review). `paths` mapping + `references` in `tsconfig.tools.json` so `tests/` scope can resolve `@lovelacer/shared`.

- [x] `pnpm test` — 99 tests across the workspace (27 analyzer + 6 shared + 66 root vitest tools), all green
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all 6 packages + tools tsconfig
- [x] `pnpm format:check` — clean
- [x] Anti-regression: integration test asserts entity haAreaId stays null even when entity's device has an area
- [x] Malformed entity_id covered for all four shapes (empty, no-dot, leading dot, trailing dot)

## Summary

body:
### Motivation
- The director `draft_plan` could be stored in `input.director_v2_package` and was not being read, causing missing draft intents.
- Draft intents can target multiple segments via `segment_ids`, which were previously ignored leading to incorrect required-ref mapping.
- Forced-primary overrides could drop the displaced primary instead of preserving it as a secondary, and diagnostics lacked per-segment visibility.
- Non-role stages were resetting role-planner markers and printing role-planner info, polluting diagnostics for unrelated stages.

### Description

body:
Addresses 8 of the actionable review comments from PR #14 (the rest were either factually incorrect, stale post-merge, or judgment-call deferrals).

### fetch_pr_pushes.py
- **`select_prs_to_fetch` filtered by `created_at` but the chart buckets by `merged_at`**, which silently dropped long-lived PRs created before `--since` but merged inside the window. Now filters by `merged_at` and skips closed-unmerged PRs (the chart uses merged-only). Removes the dead `is_merged` variable.
- **`recent_cutoff` was an isoformat() string (`+00:00`) compared lexicographically to GitHub's `closed_at` (`Z`)** → now formatted as `Z` so the comparison is correct.
- **`pr_push_events.PRIMARY KEY` extended to include `kind`** — defensive against any (theoretical) collision between a commit-SHA and a numeric force-push event id.

### backup_csvs.py
- `pr_push_events` is now exported with **deterministic ordering** `(repo, number, ts, event_id)`. Two consecutive backup runs now produce byte-identical files (verified). Eliminates noisy CSV diffs across runs.

### analyze.py
- `chart_pushes_per_pr_over_time` was **computing P25/P75 but never rendering them** — leftover from when the chart had a band (removed when switching to scatter + regression). Dead code removed.
- y-axis cap comment said "P75" but used weekly means; comment now matches code.
- Docstring updated to describe the actual visualization (scatter + regression + stats table).

### load_csv.py & data/schema.md
- PK schema updated to match.
- Schema doc clarified: open + recently-closed re-fetch only happens with `--refresh-open` (was incorrectly described as automatic).

### Not changed (with reasons)
- **Welch's t-test uses normal CDF instead of t-distribution**: with df > 1000, the difference is < 0.1%. Not worth a scipy dep.
- **`fetch_page` treats every 403 as rate-limit**: rare false positive; conservative wait-and-retry is acceptable behavior.
- **Reviewer's claim that `committed` timeline events have a top-level `created_at`**: verified via the API — they don't (only `committer.date` and `author.date`). The existing chart caveat about commit-time vs push-time is the right disclosure.

author: bryanchen-d
body:
# build(copilot): wire Turborepo cache for typecheck/lint/compile/test:unit/simulate-ci

## What

Wraps the five Copilot CI tasks under a single Turborepo entry point so Azure Pipelines can short-circuit unchanged work:

- New: [extensions/copilot/turbo.json](extensions/copilot/turbo.json) — five tasks (`typecheck`, `lint`, `compile`, `test:unit`, `simulate-ci`)
- New: [extensions/copilot/.gitignore](extensions/copilot/.gitignore) — ignore `.turbo/`
- Modified: [extensions/copilot/package.json](extensions/copilot/package.json) — add `"packageManager": "npm@10.9.2"` (required by Turbo 2.x in single-package mode)
- Modified: [build/azure-pipelines/copilot/test-steps.yml](build/azure-pipelines/copilot/test-steps.yml) — collapse five sequential `npm run` steps into one `npx turbo run ...` invocation behind a Cache@2 task

## Why

The Copilot stage currently re-runs `typecheck`, `lint`, `compile`, `test:unit`, and `simulate-ci` from scratch on every build, even when nothing relevant changed (e.g. README-only PRs, retries, partial-success retries). Turborepo content-hashes each task's declared inputs and skips work whose outputs are already in the cache.

`simulate-ci` is a safe cache target because it runs in `--ci --require-cache` mode (no network, `baseline.json` + replay cache as oracle), so its output is a deterministic function of the source + the checked-in baseline.

## Cache behavior

- **Cache key**: `"turbo-copilot" | $(Agent.OS) | $(Build.SourceBranchName) | <comma-separated input file globs>`
- **restoreKeys** fall back to the same branch prefix, then to `main`. So a fresh feature branch gets a cold-but-restored cache from `main` on its first push, and warm hits within the branch thereafter.
- **Per-branch isolation** prevents cross-PR cache pollution; the `main` fallback prevents every new branch from being fully cold.

## Verified end-to-end in CI

| Build | Scenario | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 434960 | Cold reference (npm, no Turbo) | **8m 17s** |
| 435078 | Cold Turbo, parallel | **4m 30s** (1 unrelated NOTICE flake) |
| 435121 | Re-run, populates cache | seeds Turbo cache for branch |
| 435123 | No-op README change → warm cache | **648ms · FULL TURBO · 5/5 hits** |

Estimated savings on warm cache: **~17–22 min off the Copilot stage** when nothing relevant has changed (vs cold reference).

## Risk & rollback

- **Scope**: only the Copilot stage. No effect on Linux/Darwin/Win32 product builds, signing, or artifact publishing.
- **Pre-existing fragility surfaced**: when the NOTICE step errors with `failed to get snapshot type id`, Cache@2 silently skips ALL post-job saves on that job (affects copilot-build-cache and built-in-extensions-cache too — not Turbo-specific). Turbo just experiences this as a missed cache write; the next run is cold but otherwise correct.
- **Rollback**: revert this PR. The five tasks return to running directly under `npm run`. No source code changes outside the build wrapper.

## Out of scope

- No core compile, no extension graph, no minify pipeline. Those are separate phases of the rollout (see internal planning doc).
- No new Turbo cache infrastructure — uses the existing Cache@2 backend already configured for the pipeline.

## Notes for reviewers

- The single Cache@2 + Turbo step pattern in `test-steps.yml` is the model I'd like to extend to other extensions and to root-level tasks (`hygiene`, `monaco-typecheck`, `compile-api-proposal-names`, etc.) in follow-ups.
- The `--cache-dir=.turbo` is repo-relative so the Cache@2 path matches across runs.
- `simulate-ci` declares `EXTERNAL_CACHE_LAYERS_PATH` in its env hash so external cache layer changes invalidate it correctly.

author: brianduff
body:
## Summary

cube now appends every workspace `lease`, `release`, and `force-release` to a JSON-lines audit log under `<data_dir>/audit/`. The well-known location follows the existing data-dir resolution chain (`$CUBE_DATA_DIR` → `$XDG_DATA_HOME/cube` → `~/.local/share/cube`) and sits alongside `state.db` and `locks/`.

Files are named `audit-YYYY-MM-DD.log` where the date is the Monday of the ISO week containing the event. Writes within the same week append to the same file; the first event of a new week creates a fresh file — that is the rotation. Files older than 12 weeks are pruned best-effort on each append. No external rotation crate was needed because the filename-per-period scheme handles rollover naturally and the volume is tiny (a handful of writes per workspace lifecycle).

Audit emission is best-effort: if the audit write fails (disk full, perms, etc.), cube logs a warning to stderr and continues. A failed audit must never block a lease or release.

Sample line:

```
{"event":"lease.acquired","head_commit":"abc1234","holder":"brian@host:1234","lease_id":"04dd95ca-...","repo":"mono","task":"audit smoke","ts":"2026-04-30T14:05:30Z","ts_epoch_s":1777558530,"workspace_id":"mono-agent-004"}
```

## Scope

Audited events:

- `lease.acquired` — emitted right after the lease is committed in the store (head commit recorded), before workspace setup runs.
- `lease.released` — emitted after a successful `cube workspace release`.
- `lease.force_released` — emitted after a successful `cube workspace force-release`.

Out of scope for this PR (deliberately, to keep volume low): heartbeats and TTL-based stale-lease reclamation. Both are reasonable follow-ups.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p cube` — 70 tests pass, including 7 new `audit::` unit tests covering filename derivation (Monday/Sunday/cross-week), ISO-8601 formatting, JSONL append, weekly rollover, retention pruning, and ignoring foreign files in the audit dir.
- [x] New `lease_and_release_emit_audit_log_entries` integration test in `app::tests` exercises a full lease + release through `run_with_dependencies` and asserts the audit file contains both events with the expected fields.
- [ ] Local Bazel test (`bazel test //tools/cube:cube_lib_test`) — blocked locally by an Xcode 26.3 vs 26.4 mismatch in the cached Bazel toolchain (pre-existing, unrelated). CI should be fine.

author: realmeylisdev
body:
## Description

Defense-in-depth fix for the visible "tap → optimistic flip → revert ~150 ms later" bug on likes / reposts. When the underlying publish fails (`sendLike` / `sendGenericRepost` / `deleteEvent` returns `null` or throws) and `_queueOfflineAction` is wired by the app layer, the repository now queues the action and preserves optimistic state — instead of rolling back and rethrowing.

This does **not** fix the upstream SDK regression that is the root cause (see #3741 for the full trace). It converts a UX-visible silent-revert into eventual consistency through the existing `PendingActionService` retry mechanism.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3741

## Type of Change

- [x] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Why this fix sits at the repository layer, not the SDK

Root cause is in `mobile/packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay_pool.dart`'s `_sendCollect`, where #3683 added `skipReconnect: true` to every `relay.send(...)` call without a companion path to drive reconnects when the heartbeat-induced or cold-launch `disconnected` state isn't lifted by something else. Fixing that properly is its own PR (likely either drop `skipReconnect: true` from the publish path keeping only the 5 s timeout, or wire `RelayPool` to drive proactive reconnection from `WebSocketConnectionManager.stateStream`).

This PR is intentionally narrow:
- Stops the user-visible flicker today.
- Makes the publish-result the gate, not the (currently misleading) `_isOnline()` flag.
- Behavior is unchanged for callers without `queueOfflineAction` wired (tests, non-app embedders) — the catch falls through to the original rollback + rethrow.

## What changed

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `mobile/packages/likes_repository/lib/src/likes_repository.dart` | `likeEvent` (kind-7) catch block: if `_queueOfflineAction != null`, log a warning, queue, and return placeholder; else rollback as before. Same for `unlikeEvent` (kind-5 deletion). |
| `mobile/packages/reposts_repository/lib/src/reposts_repository.dart` | Same shape for `repostVideo` (kind-16) and `unrepostVideo` (kind-5 deletion). |
| `mobile/packages/likes_repository/test/src/likes_repository_test.dart` | Extended `createRepository` helper. Added 4 new tests covering queue-on-null and queue-on-throw with the wired callback (likeEvent + unlikeEvent). Existing rollback-and-rethrow tests retained for the no-callback case. |
| `mobile/packages/reposts_repository/test/src/reposts_repository_test.dart` | Mirror of the likes test additions (4 new tests). |

No changes to BLoC, UI, providers, router, or the Nostr SDK itself. Wiring at `mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart:2432-2454` was already correct — the new path activates automatically in production.

## Verification

Local sweep on the changed packages:

```
dart format --set-exit-if-changed                         # 4 files, 0 changed
dart analyze (in packages/likes_repository)              # No issues found!
dart analyze (in packages/reposts_repository)            # No issues found!
flutter test (likes_repository)                          # 157/157 passed
flutter test (reposts_repository)                        # 114/114 passed
flutter analyze lib/blocs/video_interactions \
    test/blocs/video_interactions \
    lib/providers/app_providers.dart                     # No issues found!
flutter test test/blocs/video_interactions/              # 46/46 passed
```

## Test plan

Manual on simulator (cold-launch repro from #3741):

- [ ] Cold launch → tap heart on first For You video immediately. Heart stays red, count stays incremented.
- [ ] Background app for ~30 s → foreground → tap like. Heart stays red.
- [ ] Tap like after scrolling 5–10 s (relays connected). Indistinguishable from current happy-path behavior.
- [ ] Genuine offline path (Wi-Fi off → tap → Wi-Fi on). Existing offline branch still queues and drains.
- [ ] Repost / unrepost: same matrix.
- [ ] Like → unlike sequence: optimistic flips both directions; if both queue while online, `PendingActionService.queueAction` cancels the conflicting pair (existing logic at `pending_action_service.dart:168-188`).

## Risks and known follow-ups

1. **Eventual-consistency gap.** `PendingActionService.syncPendingActions()` only fires on `ConnectionStatusService` flip from `false → true`, on init, or on explicit external trigger. In the bug scenario the device is reported "online" the whole time, so a queued-while-online action waits for the next connectivity flap or app restart to drain. The cushion still meaningfully improves UX (no flicker; the like persists in the user's own grid; lands at the next genuine connectivity event), but does not guarantee timely server-side propagation. **Recommended follow-up:** trigger `syncPendingActions()` when any relay transitions disconnected→connected (cleanest place: a state-change stream on `RelayPool` that `PendingActionService` subscribes to). Out of scope for this PR — happy to open a tracking issue once this lands.

2. **Queued publish failures are now logged locally rather than surfaced through the BLoC error path.** When `_queueOfflineAction` is wired, the repository no longer rethrows the original publish failure, so `VideoInteractionsBloc.addError(...)` does not fire for that path. This PR now logs those handled failures with `developer.log(...)` before queueing so they remain visible in local diagnostics and exported logs without polluting Crashlytics with expected transient relay-pool noise.

3. **The upstream SDK regression remains.** This is the root cause and should be fixed in a separate PR. Two reasonable shapes:
   - Drop `skipReconnect: true` from the publish path in `_sendCollect`, keep only the 5 s `.timeout(...)`. The 5 s cap was always the real backstop — `skipReconnect: true` is over-broad and broke the "reconnect on send" contract that `WebSocketConnectionManager` documents.
   - Or have `RelayPool` listen to `stateStream` and call `relay.connect()` on `connected → disconnected` transitions. Fixes the broken contract regardless of `skipReconnect`.

4. **CHANGELOG.md not added.** Neither package has an existing CHANGELOG; the contract change is captured inline on the catch block and in this PR description. Happy to add CHANGELOGs if reviewers prefer that convention going forward.

author: cprakhar
body:
Closes #11589

### Description of change
  - For some user-defined schema (not `public`), the generated columns metadata was stored incorrectly in the metadata table. It was storing `public` in `schema` column of metadata table even when a user-defined schema was provided during `@Entity({ schema: ... })` or in `DataSourceOptions`.
  - Table path `database.schema.tablename` was being stored in `table` column of metadata table, and during `loadTables`, querying with `table: tablename` was causing a mismatch and false schema migrations.
  - For table rename and column rename, the metadata table was made to be in sync by updating the `table` or `name` column of the metadata table.
  - Removed (postgres version < 12) check in tests.
  - Updated `columnsSql` in `SqlServerQueryRunner.loadTables` to load correct `is_persisted` and `definition` for `@Entity({ database: '...', schema: '...' })`.

Users upgrading with this fix might generate migrations, as it now attempts to query against a plain table name rather than a schema- and database-qualified one.

### Pull-Request Checklist
- [x] Code is up-to-date with the `master` branch
- [x] This pull request links relevant issues as `Fixes #11589`
- [x] There are new or updated tests validating the change (`tests/**.test.ts`)

### Lodash has Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions
[CVE-2025-13465](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-13465) / [GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Lodash versions 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. An attacker can pass crafted paths which cause Lodash to delete methods from global prototypes. 

The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.  

##### Patches

This issue is patched on 4.17.23.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.9 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:L/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/E:P`

### lodash vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit`
[CVE-2026-2950](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-2950) / [GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Lodash versions 4.17.23 and earlier are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. The fix for [CVE-2025-13465](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg) only guards against string key members, so an attacker can bypass the check by passing array-wrapped path segments. This allows deletion of properties from built-in prototypes such as `Object.prototype`, `Number.prototype`, and `String.prototype`.

The issue permits deletion of prototype properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.

##### Patches

This issue is patched in 4.18.0.

##### Workarounds

None. Upgrade to the patched version.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.5 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L`

</details>

---

### lodash vulnerable to Code Injection via `_.template` imports key names
[CVE-2026-4800](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-4800) / [GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2021-23337](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) added validation for the `variable` option in `_.template` but did not apply the same validation to `options.imports` key names. Both paths flow into the same `Function()` constructor sink.

When an application passes untrusted input as `options.imports` key names, an attacker can inject default-parameter expressions that execute arbitrary code at template compilation time.

Additionally, `_.template` uses `assignInWith` to merge imports, which enumerates inherited properties via `for..in`. If `Object.prototype` has been polluted by any other vector, the polluted keys are copied into the imports object and passed to `Function()`.

##### Patches

Users should upgrade to version 4.18.0.

The fix applies two changes:
1. Validate `importsKeys` against the existing `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex (same check already used for the `variable` option)
2. Replace `assignInWith` with `assignWith` when merging imports, so only own properties are enumerated

##### Workarounds

Do not pass untrusted input as key names in `options.imports`. Only use developer-controlled, static key names.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.1 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

author: hl662
body:
## Why

`@itwin/core-common` emits two type errors into its compiled `.d.ts` files that block
consumers using `skipLibCheck: false` with TypeScript 5.8+. Both were introduced or
exposed by #7720. Neither is a runtime issue — compile-time blocker only.

**Error 1 (TS2403):** `WebAppRpcLogging.ts` had `declare global { var window: any }`
to silence a TS error on `globalThis.window` access. That declaration emits verbatim
into the compiled `.d.ts`, conflicting with the DOM lib's `Window & typeof globalThis`
for any consumer who includes `"DOM"` in their lib.

**Error 2 (TS2416):** `ResponseLike implements Response` was already a partial
contract violation before TS 5.8 (`blob`/`formData` throw, `clone` returns a shallow
spread). TypeScript 5.8 added `bytes(): Promise<Uint8Array>` to the `Body` mixin,
making the missing implementation a hard error.

## What

Two files changed, four lines net difference:

- **`WebAppRpcLogging.ts`**: remove `declare global { var window: any }` block; use
  `(globalThis as any).window` at the call site instead. Cast is compile-time only,
  produces no `.d.ts` output.

- **`RpcRequest.ts`**: drop `implements Response` from `ResponseLike`. Cast at the
  one usage site (`as unknown as Response`). `ResponseLike` is `@internal` and
  `rawResponse` — the only property that ever resolves a `ResponseLike` — has zero
  consumers in this repo, so runtime behavior is unchanged.

Adding `bytes()` was considered and rejected: `clone()`, `blob()`, and `formData()`
also violate the `Response` contract, so patching only `bytes()` keeps the lie
and defers the next Fetch spec breakage. Dropping `implements` ends it permanently.

`rawResponse`/`ResponseLike` are very highly likely dead code and will be cleaned up in a
follow-up PR.

Closes #9243

## Validation

- `rush build --to @itwin/core-common` exits zero
- `grep "declare global"` in emitted `.d.ts` files → no output
- `grep "implements"` in emitted `.d.ts` files → no output
- `rushx test` in `core/common` — 350 tests passed
- `rush extract-api --to @itwin/core-common` → diff limited to `ResponseLike` class declaration (expected, `@internal`)

body:
## Summary

Stages the cutover from `notebooks.calitp.org` to `jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov`. **Do not merge until the Cal-ITP GitHub OAuth App allows the new callback URL** — see "Pre-merge step" below.

Two coordinated changes:

### 1. Repoint `oauth_callback_url` to the new hostname

```diff
-oauth_callback_url: https://notebooks.calitp.org/hub/oauth_callback
+oauth_callback_url: https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov/hub/oauth_callback
```

Effect: every login flow — including ones initiated on the old domain — completes on the new domain. Nudges users toward `jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov` even before they update their bookmarks.

### 2. 301 redirect from notebooks.calitp.org to the new URL

Adds `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/permanent-redirect: https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov$request_uri` to the chart's nginx Ingress and removes the now-defunct `hubtest.k8s.calitp.jarv.us` hostname (replaced by the GKE Ingress in #5157).

The annotation applies to all hosts on the Ingress; after removing hubtest only `notebooks.calitp.org` remains, so the redirect's scope matches the intent.

`$request_uri` preserves the path/query — e.g. `notebooks.calitp.org/user/alice/lab/foo` → `https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov/user/alice/lab/foo`.

## Pre-merge step (one-time external action)

Add `https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov/hub/oauth_callback` to the **Cal-ITP GitHub OAuth App's** Authorization callback URL list. Keep the existing `https://notebooks.calitp.org/hub/oauth_callback` registered for now so the redirect path doesn't fail mid-flow.

OAuth App ownership / how to request changes: see #367.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Doesn't remove anything from the GitHub OAuth App's list of allowed callback URLs (the old URL stays registered until we're confident everyone's transitioned)
- Doesn't change any docs (\`docs/**\`, kubernetes README) — separate doc-cleanup PR can follow once the migration is settled
- Doesn't change DNS — `notebooks.calitp.org` keeps pointing at the nginx LB IP and serving traffic (now as a redirect)

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes
- [x] **Before merge:** GitHub OAuth App has the new callback URL added
- [ ] After merge & deploy:
  - [ ] `curl -sI https://notebooks.calitp.org/` returns 301 with `Location: https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov/`
  - [ ] Path preservation: `curl -sI https://notebooks.calitp.org/user/<name>/lab` redirects to `https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov/user/<name>/lab`
  - [ ] Login flow on `https://jupyterhub.dds.dot.ca.gov/` works end-to-end (GitHub OAuth → notebook spawn)
  - [ ] Active sessions on `notebooks.calitp.org` get redirected without losing kernel state (kernel processes are namespaced per user, not per hostname, so they should persist; cookies on the old domain become inert but redirect → re-auth on new domain → spawn returns the same user pod)

## Summary
- add `Expr.arrayElementDynamicWord` plus checked calldata/memory helpers for reading static head words from dynamic ABI array elements
- teach the macro translator to lower `(arrayElement txs idx).field` for named struct arrays with nested dynamic fields, covering an Unlink-shaped `Transaction` smoke
- document the new compiler-supported/proof-not-modeled ABI surface and keep generated axiom/interpreter matrix artifacts in sync

## Validation
- `lake build Contracts.Smoke`
- `lake build Contracts.MacroTranslateInvariantTest`
- `lake build Contracts.MacroTranslateRoundTripFuzz`
- `lake build Compiler Contracts PrintAxioms`
- `python3 scripts/generate_print_axioms.py --check`
- `make check`

Advances #1760. Does not claim the full #1760 nested-dynamic ABI definition of done: full solc differential coverage for all Unlink shapes remains follow-up work.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces new ABI decoding paths and Yul helper functions for reading words from dynamic array elements, which could affect calldata/memory safety and correctness of generated code. However, the change is scoped to new `Expr.arrayElementDynamicWord` lowering and adds targeted validation and smoke tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new compilation-model expression, `Expr.arrayElementDynamicWord`, to read **static head words** from *dynamic ABI array elements* (tuple/struct elements containing nested dynamic members), along with new checked calldata/memory Yul helpers that bounds-check the index and resolved element offsets.
> 
> Extends ABI layout utilities with `paramParentHeadWords`/`paramLocalHeadWords`, updates scope validation to use these word counts for `Expr.arrayElementWord`, and wires the new helpers into dispatch/validation and analysis passes (purity, usage, trust surface, etc.).
> 
> Enhances the macro translator to lower `(arrayElement xs i).field` on struct arrays by computing flattened head offsets; it emits `arrayElementDynamicWord` when the element type is dynamic and expands tuple destructuring to support ABI-decodable tuples with dynamic members (requiring `_` for dynamic binds). Adds a new `DynamicStructArraySmoke` contract plus invariant/round-trip coverage, and updates the interpreter/proof feature matrix and docs to mark `arrayElementDynamicWord` as compiler-supported but not modeled in proof interpreters (and excludes it from property-test generation).

author: j4rviscmd
body:
## Summary

- Replace manual `RecommendedWatcher` + 100ms batching thread with `notify-debouncer-full` (500ms debounce) for reliable event coalescing
- DELETE+CREATE event pairs from git operations (git checkout, git stash) are now automatically merged into MODIFY events at the Rust level
- This is the Rust equivalent of what `@parcel/watcher` provides in the original Electron-based VS Code

## Root Cause

PR #373 added `coalesceEvents()` on the TypeScript side, but it only works within a **single batch**. On macOS, FSEvents may deliver DELETE and CREATE events with enough delay that they land in separate 100ms batches from the Rust side. When this happens:

1. Batch 1: `[DELETE]` → TypeScript coalesces to `[DELETE]` → editor marks file orphaned
2. Batch 2: `[CREATE]` → TypeScript coalesces to `[ADDED]` → editor doesn't reconnect

The fix moves coalescing to the Rust level using `notify-debouncer-full` which accumulates events over 500ms and properly merges DELETE+CREATE pairs regardless of OS-level event delivery timing.

## Changes

- `src-tauri/src/commands/file_watcher.rs`: Full rewrite using `notify-debouncer-full`
  - Remove manual `mpsc::channel` + `std::thread::spawn` batching approach
  - Use `new_debouncer(Duration::from_millis(500), None, handler)` for intelligent coalescing
  - Simplify `WatcherHandle` to hold only the `Debouncer` instance
  - Keep TypeScript-side `coalesceEvents()` as a defensive fallback (no TS changes needed)

## Test Plan

- [x] Open a git-tracked file in the editor, make a change and save it
- [x] Run `Git: Discard Changes` from the command palette
- [x] Verify the editor tab immediately shows the reverted content
- [x] Repeat with `git checkout -- file` from a terminal
- [ ] On macOS, verify files with non-ASCII characters are correctly detected
- [x] Verify normal file save/edit detection still works (within ~500ms latency)

Closes #366

author: idan-rubin
body:
## Why

Two threads converged into this PR:

1. A regression in `0.17.0` where `BrowserClaw.launch({ url })` opened the page but didn't load the URL — the visible startup tab stayed on `about:blank` while the URL ended up in a different tab.
2. The JPM-14751 demo session (2026-04-30) surfaced 4 additional reliability issues affecting headed-Chrome workflows.

This PR ships fixes for all of them in one batch, with new tests and a minor version bump to **0.18.0**.

## What changed

### 1. Launch URL no longer loads in the wrong tab (regression fix)

Commit `0a43381` ("Slim Chrome flags and make stealth opt-in") removed `--disable-features=Translate,MediaRouter` and other flags from the default launch path. Without those, headed Chrome surfaces `chrome://omnibox-popup-*` as a CDP `type=page` target. The picker (`pickActiveTargetId`) treated it as the "first non-blank" page, `goto(url)` ran on the WebUI overlay, and Chrome opened the URL in a separate tab — leaving the visible about:blank tab unchanged.

**Fix:** `getAllPages` filters `chrome://omnibox-popup` URLs out of every CDP page enumeration. One change covers `currentPage()`, `tabs()`, `waitForTab()`, and every other path that enumerates tabs.

### 2. `BrowserClaw.focus(targetId)` now activates the macOS window

Playwright's `Page.bringToFront()` activates a tab inside Chrome's window stack but doesn't raise the OS window above other apps on macOS. Demo viewers saw the wrong Chrome window in the foreground despite the script's page reference being correct.

**Fix:** on darwin, `focus()` follows up with `osascript` activation by chrome's pid (`tell application "System Events" to set frontmost of (first process whose unix id is <pid>) to true`). Pid-based avoids hardcoding the app name (Chrome / Chromium / Edge / Brave). New exported helper `activateMacOsWindowByPid` (async, best-effort).

### 3. `screenshot({ timeoutMs })`

Playwright's screenshot internally awaits font loading; when external fonts are slow, it hangs for the default 30s. The previous browserclaw `ScreenshotOptions` had no way to bound this.

**Fix:** new `ScreenshotOptions.timeoutMs` (also accepted by `screenshotWithLabels`) forwards to Playwright's `page.screenshot({ timeout })`. Pass a small value to fail fast on font hangs, or `0` to disable the wait entirely.

### 4. `Default/Sessions/*` no longer compounds across runs

Chrome session-restore files (`Tabs_NNN`, `Session_NNN`, `Current Session`, `Current Tabs`, `Last Session`, `Last Tabs`) accumulated in the user-data-dir across runs. Subsequent launches restored those tabs, surfacing extra targets the script didn't expect.

**Fix:** `ensureCleanExit` now also wipes session-restore files on every launch via the new exported `wipeChromeSessionState`. Cookies, preferences, and other persistent state are preserved.

### 5. `launchChrome` auto-picks a free CDP port

Hard-killed Chrome processes can leave port 9222 held briefly, causing `connectOverCDP: ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9222` on the next launch.

**Fix:** when the caller doesn't pin `cdpPort`, `launchChrome` iterates from 9222 (`reservePortStartingAt`, scans up to 20 ports) until a free one is found. Explicit `opts.cdpPort` still enforces the requested port.

## Tests

- `connection.test.ts`: 1 new `getAllPages` test verifying omnibox-popup targets are filtered while legit `chrome://settings`-style pages remain selectable.
- `chrome-launcher.test.ts`: 6 new tests — `wipeChromeSessionState` (2), `reservePortStartingAt` (2), `activateMacOsWindowByPid` (2).
- `browser.test.ts`: 2 new tests verifying `screenshot({ timeoutMs })` is forwarded to the underlying call.
- Manual smoke: `BrowserClaw.launch({ url, headless: false, isolated: true })` against `https://playwright.dev/` returns a 173-ref ARIA snapshot and `tabs()` reports a single visible tab.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm test` — 17,536/17,536 passing
- [x] `npx eslint src/` clean
- [x] `npm run format:check` clean
- [x] Headed manual smoke against playwright.dev (snapshot rendered, currentPage URL matches)

## Version

`0.17.0` → **`0.18.0`** (minor — new exports + new options + new observable behavior in `focus()`, `launch()`, `screenshot()`).

## Out of scope

- Attached browsers (`BrowserClaw.connect`) don't get macOS OS-level activation because we don't know the chrome pid for an externally-launched instance.
- Multi-profile (`Profile 1/`, `Profile 2/`) Chrome data dirs aren't covered by the session wipe — only `Default/`. browserclaw's typical use is single-profile.

author: he-pin
body:
## Summary

This PR adds array-level lazy views for large `std.map`, `std.mapWithIndex`, and non-constant `std.makeArray` results.

The old representation eagerly allocated one `LazyApply1`/`LazyApply2` per element. For large arrays this burns allocation even when callers only force a small suffix/prefix. The new representation keeps the callback and evaluation context once per array, computes elements on demand, and caches computed values.

Important JVM/JIT/GC choices:

- Keep the old flat `Array[LazyApply*]` representation below `LAZY_VIEW_THRESHOLD = 4096`, where the JVM is usually better off with the simple monomorphic layout.
- Materialize back to `Array[Eval]` from `asLazyArray` so existing full-array stdlib consumers remain stack-safe and predictable.
- `std.reverse(lazyView)` materializes before reversing so the original and reversed arrays share the same element thunks; this preserves trace/native callback semantics and avoids duplicate evaluation.
- Release captured evaluator/function state after full materialization.

## Correctness Coverage

Added directional tests for selective forcing and a trace regression covering the reverse-cache behavior for all three lazy view subclasses:

- `MakeArrayArr`
- `MappedArr`
- `MappedWithIndexArr`

Also added `bench/resources/sjsonnet_suite/lazy_array_sparse_indexing.jsonnet`, a reproducible sparse-indexing workload for the benchmark harness.

## JMH

Environment: JMH 1.37, Mill JVM `zulu:21`, `-wi 3 -i 5 -w 1s -r 2s -f 1 -tu ms`. Baseline is `upstream/master` at `3a9a4928`; benchmark files introduced by this PR were passed to master by absolute path for the baseline run. This sweep was rerun after the lazy-array hot-path fix in `65840c5c`.

| `bench/resources/cpp_suite/realistic2.jsonnet` | `44.530 ± 0.685 ms/op` | `39.766 ± 0.661 ms/op` | 1.12x faster |
| `bench/resources/go_suite/foldl.jsonnet` | `0.070 ± 0.001 ms/op` | `0.072 ± 0.001 ms/op` | neutral |
| `bench/resources/sjsonnet_suite/lazy_array_sparse_indexing.jsonnet` | `20.023 ± 4.123 ms/op` | `3.488 ± 0.135 ms/op` | 5.74x faster |
| `bench/resources/go_suite/reverse.jsonnet` | `6.434 ± 0.224 ms/op` | `5.001 ± 0.150 ms/op` | 1.29x faster |
| `bench/resources/go_suite/base64_byte_array.jsonnet` | `0.749 ± 0.037 ms/op` | `0.748 ± 0.042 ms/op` | neutral |

author: sam-at-luther
body:
## Summary

Stacked on **PR #58** (\`feature/insideout-import-phase1\`). Two surgical P1 fixes from the qa-professor review of #58, plus a follow-up round addressing the QA review of this PR. Targets PR #58's branch directly so the fixes land **with** PR #58 when the maintainer merges.

Same theme as #187: \"no silent state.\" Two related changes:

### 1. Symmetric tag-error policy across discoverers [P1]

CloudWatchLogs swallowed \`ListTagsForResource\` errors and emitted the resource with empty tags. Lambda / SQS / DynamoDB all fail-loud (SecretsManager has no separate tag call — its tags are inline). The asymmetry produced two real bugs:

1. **With \`--tags\` filtering**: a resource whose tags couldn't be fetched silently dropped from the output, giving a false-negative on tag-based scoping.
2. **Without \`--tags\` filtering**: the resource emitted with empty tags, giving a misleading "no tags" report when tags were just inaccessible.

CWL now matches its siblings: tag-fetch errors abort discovery with a wrapped error that names the failing log group.

### 2. \`FilterImportBlocks\` escalates dropped + tracks malformed [P1]

\`FilterImportBlocks\` silently dropped import blocks whose target resource didn't exist in the generated HCL. The cited rationale was real ("prevents 'Configuration for import target does not exist' errors"), but silent drops produced a stack where:

- The consuming HCL still referenced the un-importable target as a literal ARN.
- \`imports.tf\` no longer had the corresponding import block.
- \`terraform validate\` passed.
- \`terraform apply\` failed at runtime.

Fix:

- \`FilterImportBlocks\` returns \`(filtered, dropped, malformed, err)\`. \`dropped\` is well-formed targets the dep chase missed; \`malformed\` is parse-level anomalies (missing \`to\` attr, unparseable traversal). Tracked separately so a regression in extractTraversalAddress doesn't masquerade as "dep chase did its job."
- \`Result\` gains \`DroppedImports\` and \`MalformedImports\` so callers / CI see them programmatically.
- The runner Warn-logs each entry at the time of filtering (with cause classes + remediation), then **escalates** to a wrapped error at the end of \`Run()\` if either list is non-empty. Wrappers and CI scripts now see a non-zero exit instead of having to log-scrape.
- HCL behavior unchanged.

## QA-pass-2 fixes (commit \`ee89c5e\`)

A second qa-professor review on the first version of this PR caught:

- **[P1]** Warn-only was "logged into the void" — runner now escalates.
- **[P2]** Malformed \`to\` was lumped in with dropped targets — now tracked separately.
- **[P2]** SecretsManager symmetry claim was wrong (no separate tag call) — corrected in code comments and PR body.
- **[P2]** Test used substring matching against \`hclwrite\` output — now parses HCL with the production helper.
- **[P2]** Warn message lacked actionability — added cause classes + remediation steps.

body:
## Summary
Makes the `initial_prompt` vocabulary bias configurable per machine via a plain-text file (`~/.meeting-capture/vocab.txt`) and a new `meeting-capture vocab` CLI subcommand. Different machines / projects need different proper-noun and acronym lists; editing a launchd plist or shell profile to set an env var is awkward, so this surfaces it as first-class daemon configuration.

## Behavior
The daemon re-reads the file on every chunk, so edits apply immediately — no restart needed.

Resolution order (most → least specific):

1. Explicit `initial_prompt=...` argument to `transcribe()`
2. `~/.meeting-capture/vocab.txt`
3. `MEETING_CAPTURE_WHISPER_PROMPT` env var
4. Built-in default

An empty file is treated as explicit opt-out — Whisper runs without a prompt. Useful when the bias hurts more than it helps on a given machine's audio.

## CLI
```
meeting-capture vocab          show effective prompt and source
meeting-capture vocab edit     open in $EDITOR (seeded with default on first edit)
meeting-capture vocab clear    remove the file (fall back to env / default)
meeting-capture vocab path     print the path (for piping)
```

`meeting-capture doctor` now also reports the active model and which source the prompt resolved from.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 31 tests pass; new code is exercised by the CLI.
- [x] `meeting-capture vocab` (no file) — reports `built-in default`.
- [x] After writing a custom file — reports `vocab file (...)` and the new content.
- [x] `meeting-capture vocab path` — prints the file path.
- [x] Daemon picks up edits within one chunk cycle (no restart needed) — verified by reading `transcriber.resolved_prompt()` after writes.

body: ## Summary Sprint acotado que cierra los dos 🔴 secundarios del review de PR #29 (HU-005) que el fundador difirió explícitamente al mergear. Ambos son hardenings de `public.tournament_registrations` — **sin cambios de producto, UI ni de la API TS**. **Migración única**: `apps/web/supabase/migrations/20260430140000_g4_sprint6_hotfixes_registrations.sql`. ### 🔴 1 · Trigger `sync_tournament_slots_on_status_change` sin validación de torneo abierto El INSERT trigger `enforce_tournament_capacity` sí validaba `v_status = 'abierto_inscripciones'` desde HU-005, pero el UPDATE trigger no. Esto permitía que una inscripción ya creada se re-confirmara (via `cancelada|lista_espera → confirmada`) después de que el torneo pasara a `cerrado_inscripciones`/`cancelado`/`finalizado`, saltándose la ventana de inscripción. **Fix:** `create or replace function` que lee `status` bajo el mismo `for update` y hace `raise exception 'tournament_not_open' using errcode = 'P0001'` cuando la transición es a `confirmada` sobre un torneo cerrado. El camino opuesto (`confirmada → !confirmada`) queda libre de check: cancelar un inscripto en un torneo ya cerrado tiene que seguir siendo legítimo. ### 🔴 2 · RLS `tr_update_self_or_owner` sin `WITH CHECK` por rol La policy tenía solo `USING` y PostgreSQL defaulteaba `WITH CHECK` al mismo `USING`. Como `registered_by` no cambia durante un update, cualquier usuario que fuera `registered_by` podía setear **cualquier** `status` desde un cliente Supabase directo (auto-promoción de `lista_espera`/`cancelada` a `confirmada`). **Fix:** `drop + create policy` con `WITH CHECK` explícito que documenta el contrato: - **Rama promotor**: `tournaments.owner_id = auth.uid()` → puede setear `confirmada`/`lista_espera`/`cancelada`. - **Rama self**: `registered_by = auth.uid() AND status = 'cancelada'` → cualquier otro destino cae fuera del check y RLS lo rechaza. - `comment on policy` documenta la regla para que futuras migraciones la respeten. Las dos reglas se complementan: el trigger valida el estado del torneo al re-confirmar, RLS restringe qué status puede setear cada rol. Redundancia intencional para defensa en profundidad. ### Backend / Frontend — sin tocar `mapRegistrationError` ya mapeaba `P0001/tournament_not_open` a "El torneo no está abierto a inscripciones." desde HU-005, así que el nuevo raise del trigger se reporta al usuario con texto humano sin tocar una línea de TS. ### Tests No se agregan tests nuevos: los fixes son DB-only (trigger + RLS) y se validan E2E en QA (G5), no en vitest con mocks. Los 153 tests existentes siguen pasando. ### Validación local | Check | Resultado | |---|---| | `pnpm lint` (apps/web) | 0 errors · 15 warnings (preexistentes) | | `pnpm typecheck` | OK | | `pnpm test` | **153/153** PASS | | `pnpm build` | OK (sin rutas nuevas) | ### Documentación sincronizada - `tasks/gate-status.md`: G4 pasa a "Sprint 6" con nota del hotfix. - `tasks/sprint-week-06.md` (nuevo): alcance + diff semántico + deuda técnica restante. - `tasks/hu/HU-005.md`: evidencias con PR #29 merged + descripción de los dos hardenings. - `memory/daily/2026-04-30.md` (nuevo): bitácora del sprint. ### Deuda técnica registrada (no atacada en este PR) - **6 findings menores de Devin Review en PR #30**: la UI `app.devin.ai/review/...` devolvía 500 al cargar el detalle, y la API pública de GitHub solo expone el 🔴 crítico (ya resuelto). Se retomará en G5 QA cuando Devin Review restablezca la UI o por review manual. - **Migración consolidada**: validar en ambiente limpio que Sprint 5 + Sprint 6 produce el mismo esquema que un full rebuild desde scratch antes de cerrar G4. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Verificar en un ambiente Supabase (local o staging) que aplicar la migración nueva sobre un snapshot post-Sprint 5 no rompe inscripciones existentes (función `create or replace` sobre trigger vivo, policy drop+create). - [ ] Ejercer desde un cliente Supabase con JWT de un `registered_by` normal (no promotor): intentar `update tournament_registrations set status='confirmada'` sobre una fila propia en `lista_espera` → debe fallar con RLS (antes pasaba). - [ ] Ejercer el re-confirm: con un torneo en `cerrado_inscripciones` + una inscripción `cancelada`, el promotor intenta llevarla a `confirmada` → ahora debe fallar con `tournament_not_open` (antes pasaba silenciosamente). Cancelar una `confirmada` en torneo cerrado debe seguir funcionando. - [ ] Confirmar desde la UI (`/tournaments/[id]/register`, `/tournaments/[id]/registrations`) que el flujo normal (inscribirse en torneo abierto, cancelar como capitán, promotor moviendo entre `confirmada`/`lista_espera`) sigue comportándose igual. ### Notes Sprint 6 es explícitamente un hotfix de deuda técnica — no agrega features ni cambia contratos públicos. author: romaine-life-app[bot]
body:
Closes items 2 and 3 of the PR #170 failure-chain triage. (Item 1 — agent misread the screenshot — landed in PR #171.)

## Why

PR #170 verification passed and shipped a screenshot showing `vigor gained: 88` for an Akabeko start-of-combat trigger that should have produced exactly 8. Two structural gaps after the agent's misread:

- **`must_show` was loose**: "non-zero count, at minimum 8 after first combat-start trigger" accepts ≥ 8, so a literal-reading wrapper would pass `88` even with a perfectly-honest agent.
- **`Apply-VerificationEvidenceGuard` had no field to compare**: it checks `text_visible:true` and non-empty `observed_text`, but never compares observed against any expected value the test plan declared.

## What this PR does

**Schema:** screenshot `required_evidence` items with `text_visible_required:true` must now also carry a literal `expected_text` field. The wrapper does a case-insensitive, word-boundary-aware substring match between `observed_text` and `expected_text` and aborts with `claimed_result_not_observed` on mismatch.

**Word-boundary matching matters**: a naive `.Contains()` lets `vigor gained: 8` match `vigor gained: 88` as a prefix. Pattern is `(?:^|[^A-Za-z0-9]) + escape(needle) + (?:[^A-Za-z0-9]|$)` so the needle must sit between non-alphanumerics or string ends — a trailing digit can't extend without breaking the boundary rule.

**Test-plan prompt** now forbids loose phrasings ("non-zero", "at minimum N", "≥ N", "N or cumulative") and requires `expected_text` derived from `scenario_setup × validation_plan`, e.g. `vigor gained: 8` for *one* combat-start of Akabeko. If the test plan can't pin a specific expected value because the implementation behavior is genuinely ambiguous, the rule is to abort with `validation_plan_impossible` rather than ship a loose contract.

**Verification prompt** now requires copying literal screenshot characters into `observed_text` — not paraphrased, not "cleaned up". If the agent can't read the value confidently, abort with `target_evidence_missing` rather than guess what the contract said it should show.

## Tests

`EvidenceGuard.Tests.ps1` exercises the comparison logic — including the specific PR #170 failure (`8` must not match `88`), digit-extension cases (`8` must not match `80` or `800`), full-string equality, start-anchor, end-anchor, missing-text, empty-observed, and case-insensitivity. Suite is 53/53.

## Doc

`docs/issue-agent.md`: new "Expected-Value Contract on Required Evidence" section describing the rule, the derivation principle (compute from scenario × validation plan), and the forbidden loose phrasings.

## What's still deferred

The Akabeko 11×-per-combat fire is a real implementation bug in PR #170. Worth a follow-up issue against that PR — but that's the bug this contract would have caught at verification time, not this PR's scope.

author: srotzin
body:
hive-rosetta is a small open-source EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization signer published under the same name on both registries, MIT-licensed.

- NPM: https://www.npmjs.com/package/hive-rosetta
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/hive-rosetta/
- Source: https://github.com/srotzin/hive-rosetta

Why it might be useful in this list:

1. Same import name across Node and Python. `npm i hive-rosetta` and `pip install hive-rosetta` both expose an identical signer surface, so polyglot teams can copy/paste the same example into either runtime.
2. Zero web3 dependency. The Node package uses `@noble/curves` + `@noble/hashes` only. EIP-712 domain separator and struct hash are computed from primitives. Node version: 7.1KB signer.js.
3. Primitives-only EIP-712. The TypedData encoding is implemented inline so a reviewer can read the entire signing path in one file. The Python port uses `eth_keys` for the secp256k1 step but keeps the EIP-712 encoder hand-rolled to stay byte-identical with Node.
4. Wire shape matches the spec. Output is `{scheme: 'exact', network: 'eip155:8453', payload: {authorization: {from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce}, signature}}` — drops directly into `/verify` and `/settle` on any spec-compliant facilitator.
5. Cross-language determinism is verified: same private key produces the same checksummed Ethereum address and the same digest from both languages.

Tests: 39 passing in the Node package (canonical typehash check, deterministic signing for fixed inputs, tampering rejection, etc.). Python port has its own pytest suite.

License: MIT. Free forever.

Happy to revise wording or placement to fit the list's conventions.

author: alistair3149
body:
## Summary

The dispatcher's OAuth gate (`src/runtime/dispatcher.ts`) fires on every tool call when the active wiki has `oauth2ClientId` set, regardless of whether the tool actually authenticates against that wiki. This bypass adds 5 tool names that never need an active-wiki token:

- `add-wiki` — registers a new wiki; doesn't authenticate against the active one
- `set-wiki` — changes registry state; the outgoing wiki's OAuth shouldn't be required to leave it
- `remove-wiki` — changes registry state
- `oauth-status` / `oauth-logout` — manage the OAuth token store; must work even when OAuth is broken

## The bug it fixes

Without this, a wiki whose OAuth has gone stale renders the five tools above unreachable. Specifically: calling `set-wiki` to switch *away* from the broken wiki still triggers the gate on the *outgoing* (broken) wiki, returns `401`, and leaves the user with no way to escape. Same for `oauth-logout`, which is supposed to be the recovery tool but itself goes through the same gate.

Encountered while smoke-testing #340 against `starcitizen.tools`: my session's default wiki had `oauth2ClientId` set with an unreachable token endpoint, blocking every tool call including `set-wiki` to a different wiki.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` → 843/843 pass (5 new parameterised tests added; one per bypass tool name verifying the handler runs even when the active wiki is OAuth-configured against an unreachable token endpoint)
- [x] `npm run lint` → clean
- [x] `npm run build` → clean
- [x] **Live verify**: with the active wiki configured for OAuth (any `oauth2ClientId` will do) and the token endpoint reachable or not, confirm `set-wiki` to a different wiki succeeds without an OAuth roundtrip.

body:
## Summary

End-to-end MVP for **ClipGenius AI** — turns long-form videos into 9:16 short clips, dubs them in any language, and schedules them to YouTube Shorts / Instagram Reels. Implemented entirely on a **free open-source stack** (no paid APIs).

**Live deployments**
- Frontend (Vercel): https://clipgenius-ai-delta.vercel.app — set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://rah7809-clipgenius-api.hf.space` and redeploy. The frontend code falls back to that URL by default if the env var is missing, so a redeploy is sufficient.
- Backend (HuggingFace Spaces, free CPU, 16 GB RAM): https://rah7809-clipgenius-api.hf.space (`/health`, `/docs`)
- HF Space dashboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/rah7809/clipgenius-api

**Verified working end-to-end** on the live HF deploy (see test-results comment on this PR): a 49-second video uploaded through the dashboard becomes 8 vertical 720×1280 clips with burned captions and Hindi `edge-tts` dubs in ~70 seconds. All 6 adversarial assertions passed.

### Free pipeline (no API keys required)
- **Transcription**: `faster-whisper` (tiny, ~75 MB model, CPU-only)
- **Translation**: `deep-translator` (free Google Translate endpoint)
- **TTS for dubs**: `edge-tts` (free Microsoft Edge TTS, 60+ languages)
- **Captions / hashtags**: heuristic generator on the transcript (no LLM)
- **Viral-moment scoring**: audio RMS + curated keyword lexicon + pause patterns
- **Vertical reframe**: OpenCV Haar cascade face-tracking + ffmpeg `-preset ultrafast` at 720×1280
- OpenAI key is still wired in code as an optional enhancement; gracefully falls back to the free stack when unset.

### What's in this PR
- `backend/` — FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Celery worker + Beat. Routers for auth, videos, clips, schedule, integrations, files. Services for `free_stack` (faster-whisper / deep-translator / edge-tts), yt-dlp, ffmpeg/OpenCV reframe-and-caption, S3 storage with local fallback, and YouTube/Meta posting.
- `frontend/` — Next.js 14 (app router) + Tailwind + SWR. Defaults `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` to the live HF URL, and resolves backend-supplied relative `/api/v1/files/...` clip URLs through the API base via `mediaUrl()` (commit `f4d07d7`, fixes a bug found during this session's testing).
- `backend/Dockerfile` + `start_all.sh` — single-container variant that runs API + worker + beat + an embedded `redis-server` together (used on HuggingFace Spaces; flip `EMBED_REDIS=0` / `BUNDLED_WORKERS=0` and use `render.yaml` on a paid host).
- DB models switched from `postgresql.UUID` to `sqlalchemy.types.Uuid` so the same code runs on Postgres and the SQLite default on HF.
- `render.yaml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, comprehensive `README.md`.

### Known limitations (also in README)
- **No lip-sync** — dubbing replaces the audio track only.
- **Engagement detection is heuristic**, not a trained model.
- **YouTube URL ingestion is blocked by YouTube's datacenter-IP bot detection** — use file upload instead. Same downstream pipeline.
- **YouTube + Meta auto-posting** code is production-correct but won't reach non-tester accounts until you complete each platform's app verification.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Rotate the Render + Vercel + HuggingFace tokens you pasted earlier in chat** — they are in the session transcript and should be revoked. Render and Vercel are not strictly required by the live deploy anymore, but the HF token still has Spaces write access on your account.
- [ ] Update Vercel env `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://rah7809-clipgenius-api.hf.space` and trigger a redeploy. (Optional — the frontend code defaults to this URL, but setting the env explicitly is cleaner and lets you point at a paid backend later without a code change.)
- [ ] Sign up on https://clipgenius-ai-delta.vercel.app/signup with a fresh email, upload a short video file (skip the YouTube URL field — it's bot-detected), wait ~1–2 min on the project page, and verify 5–10 clip cards render with `ready` status, real transcript-derived titles, burned captions, and a Hindi dub when you switch the language dropdown.
- [ ] If you want auto-posting to actually publish, finish the YouTube OAuth verification (Google Cloud → enable YouTube Data API v3 → OAuth 2.0 Web client, redirect URI `https://rah7809-clipgenius-api.hf.space/api/v1/integrations/youtube/callback`) and the Meta app review (developers.facebook.com → Instagram Graph API product, redirect URI `https://rah7809-clipgenius-api.hf.space/api/v1/integrations/instagram/callback`). Provide the resulting client ID/secret pairs and they'll auto-wire on next backend deploy.
- [ ] Decide whether to add AWS S3 credentials (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_S3_BUCKET`, `AWS_REGION`) for permanent clip storage. The HF Space currently uses local-disk fallback, which works for the lifetime of the container but won't survive a HF rebuild and isn't fetchable by Instagram for cross-platform posting.
- [ ] Decide whether to stay on the HF free CPU tier or move to a paid host (e.g. Render Starter — `render.yaml` is in the repo) for higher concurrency / per-user isolation.

### Notes

- Backend auth uses `bcrypt` directly (not `passlib`) because `passlib` 1.7.4 + `bcrypt` 4.1+ raise `ValueError: password cannot be longer than 72 bytes` at module init. Fixed in commit `7c3cb14`.
- The HF Space runs API + worker + beat + an embedded `redis-server` in one container via `start_all.sh` so it works on the free CPU tier without managed Redis. To split services on a paid host, set `EMBED_REDIS=0`, `BUNDLED_WORKERS=0`, and use `render.yaml`.
