Plan śledzący: `.ai/runs/2026-05-03-partner-master-phase-1-tax-identity.md`
Status: w trakcie

## Cel

Wprowadzić additive-only schemat Fazy 1, API, command pattern, ACL, słowniki, encryption coverage, i18n oraz minimalny widget injection dla migracji Partner Master w module `customers` — bez migracji danych istniejących rekordów.

## Co się zmieniło

- **Encje:** nowa tabela `customer_tax_identities` z kompozytowym partial unique index (`country_code`, `kind`, `value`) `where deleted_at is null`; trzy nowe nullowalne kolumny tekstowe na `customer_companies` (`legal_form`, `entity_type`, `full_address_krs`) plus relacja `OneToMany taxIdentities` na `CustomerEntity`.
- **Walidatory:** czyste helpery checksum w `data/taxIdentityChecksums.ts` (NIP modulo-11, REGON 9- i 14-cyfrowy weighted, KRS length, PESEL modulo-10 z walidacją kalendarzową, format VAT EU per kraj) oraz schematy zod (`nipSchema`, `regonSchema`, `krsSchema`, `peselSchema`, `vatEuSchema`, `taxIdentityCreateSchema`, `taxIdentityUpdateSchema`, `taxIdentityDeleteSchema`) podpięte do kluczy tłumaczeń.
- **Testy unit:** przypadki pozytywne i negatywne dla każdego helpera oraz schematów zod create/update w `packages/core/src/modules/customers/__tests__/taxIdentityChecksums.test.ts` oraz `validators.taxIdentity.test.ts`.
- **Module wiring:** `acl.ts` (`customers.tax_identities.{view,manage}`), `setup.ts` (employee dostaje `view`), `events.ts` (`customers.tax_identity.{created,updated,deleted}`), `encryption.ts` (pole `value` na nowej tabeli + `full_address_krs` na profilu firmy), `customFieldDefaults.ts` i `ce.ts` (domyślne pola własne + rejestracja encji), `cli.ts` (`LEGAL_FORM_DEFAULTS` i `ENTITY_TYPE_DEFAULTS` seedowane wewnątrz `seedCustomerDictionaries`), oraz allow-list rodzajów słowników w `commands/shared.ts` i `data/validators.ts`.
- **Komendy:** `commands/taxIdentities.ts` z create / update / delete, snapshot-based undo, soft-delete przez `deletedAt`, scope guards (tenant + organization), eventy query-index oraz tłumaczenie błędu Postgres unique-violation na HTTP 409.
- **API:** `api/companies/[id]/tax-identities/route.ts` (GET list + POST create) oraz `api/companies/[id]/tax-identities/[tid]/route.ts` (PATCH + DELETE). Oba pliki przepuszczają operacje przez command bus, zwracają 404 / 403 / 422 w odpowiednich przypadkach. PATCH odrzuca `value` bez `kind`, żeby checksum nie mogła zostać obejście.

author: say-5
body:
Fixes #64.

`HandleSubscribe` spawns a goroutine that calls `Consumer.ReplayEvents`, which opens a pebble `Iterator` over `UncompressedDB`/`CompressedDB`. On shutdown `cmd/jetstream/main.go` calls `c.Shutdown()` (which only drained the sequencer) and then immediately calls `UncompressedDB.Close()` / `CompressedDB.Close()`. Any replay goroutine still inside `iter.Next()` then dereferences a freed sstable reader, producing the panic in the issue (`pkg/server/server.go:221` -> `pkg/consumer/persist.go:183` -> `pebble/sstable/reader.go:567`).

The websocket `defer ws.Close()` does not stop the replay goroutine; it is fire-and-forget, so the iterator can outlive both the request context's effective use and the surrounding handler.

Fix: give `Consumer` a dedicated replay context plus a `sync.WaitGroup`. `ReplayEvents` registers itself before opening an iterator, bails out early if shutdown has already started, and merges the consumer's replay context into the iterator's context so blocking pebble calls unwind on shutdown. `Shutdown` cancels the replay context after the sequencer drains and waits (with a 10s timeout) for every in-flight replay to release its iterator before returning. Callers (existing `main.go`) then close the pebble DBs as before, with no race.

Also adds two regression tests run under `-race`:
- `TestReplayEventsShutdownRace` spawns 16 concurrent replays against both DBs, calls `Shutdown`, then closes the pebble DBs and asserts no panic and that all replays unwind.
- `TestReplayEventsRejectsAfterShutdown` confirms a late `ReplayEvents` call returns `context.Canceled` instead of opening an iterator against DBs the caller is about to close.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -race ./pkg/server/... ./pkg/consumer/...` all pass locally on go1.26.2.

body:
## Summary

Reframes the plugin so a marketplace install delivers meaningful protection
without any configuration, while preserving the runtime upgrade path.

- **Built-in deny defaults** in `policy-guard.sh` for sensitive reads
  (`.env`, `.ssh/`, `.aws/`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `secrets/`,
  `credentials/`, `config/database.yml`, `config/credentials.json`,
  `config/master.key`, `.npmrc`/`.pypirc`/`.netrc`, `.gcp/`, `gcloud/`),
  sensitive writes (above + `.github/workflows/`), and dangerous bash
  commands (`rm -rf /`, `git push --force`, `curl|sh`, `chmod 777`,
  `mkfs*`, `dd if=`, fork bombs). `sudo` warns by default.
- `[mode]` (`strict`/`balanced`/`permissive`) and `[allow]` exemptions
  in `.symbiont/local-policy.toml`. Local rules **extend** the built-ins.
- New slash commands: `/symbi-protect`, `/symbi-disable`, `/symbi-enable`.
- `scripts/lib/json-extract.sh` shared field extractor with three
  backends (jq → python3 → narrow bash awk fallback). Drops the hard
  `jq` dependency.
- Sensitive-file nudge in `install-check.sh` at session start.
- `audit-log.sh` always logs (no longer gated on `symbiont.toml`).
- Hook matchers extended to include `Read` and `MultiEdit`.
- Every hook honors a `.symbiont/disabled` kill switch.
- README rewritten to lead with the plugin-only flow; Cedar/ORGA/Mode B
  moved below a "Going further" heading.
- 78-case bash test suite under `tests/` covering built-ins, backend
  parity, chain-bypass resistance, allowlist exemptions, mode switching,
  and the kill switch.

Bash deny patterns match against the **full** command string so chain
prefixes (`true && true && rm -rf /`) still trigger. The hook does
not parse shell syntax — string-contains is sufficient and avoids the
shell-AST rabbit hole.

No new dependency on the `symbi` runtime binary. Tier 3 Cedar
evaluation lights up automatically when `symbi` is on PATH; nothing
in this PR requires it.

- [x] `bash tests/run-tests.sh` — 78/78 passing
- [x] `shellcheck scripts/*.sh scripts/lib/*.sh tests/*.sh` — clean
- [x] Smoke: `install-check.sh` on empty/sensitive/disabled/policy-present projects
- [x] Smoke: `policy-guard.sh` blocks `.env` read with exit 2
- [x] Smoke: `audit-log.sh` writes JSONL line

author: atimics
body:
## Summary

Stacks on #30. Same root cause, second layer: even with the API key safe in `localStorage`, the player's character was still dying on every server restart because `RubyHighService` keeps `QuizState` in-memory by default and the DynamoDB backend is opt-in. Same fix shape — client owns the truth.

## Server

- `SessionTelemetry` gains a `snapshot: ClientStateSnapshot` field. Versioned (`v: 1`) opaque blob containing the durable bits of `QuizState`: character, `currentGrade`, `completedGrades`, `askedQuestionIds`, `npcRosters`, `npcCohort`, `mentorOffer`, `hasSeenIntro`, faculty, subject. Round-local fields (current question, `activeRound`, `lastReveal`, `score`) are intentionally excluded — you pick back up between rounds, not mid-question.
- New `POST /session/<id>/hydrate` accepts `{ snapshot }` and dispatches to a new `RubyHighService.hydrateFromSnapshot()`. The service refuses to overwrite a bucket that already has a character (guard against a stale tab clobbering active play). Returns the rebuilt session state so the client doesn't need a follow-up GET.

## Client

- New `STATE_KEY = "rh_quiz_state_v1"` localStorage slot, with `saveStateSnapshot` / `loadStateSnapshot` / `clearStateSnapshot` helpers next to the auth ones.
- `render(s)` now calls `saveStateSnapshot(t)` on every successful telemetry. Cheap, idempotent, the snapshot the server would have built on the next GET anyway.
- Boot path swapped from `fetchSession()` to `bootSession()`: GET first; if the server returns no character and `localStorage` has a snapshot, POST `/hydrate`, render the rebuilt response. Covers server restart, fresh cookie, dev reset.
- Snapshot is cleared on character reroll (before the `clear-character` command, to avoid a hydrate race) and on logout (so the next sign-in starts genuinely clean).

## What this doesn't include

- **No cloud sync.** Per direction — pure localStorage for now. Multi-device support is a future concern (probably "registration or something" later, per the brief).
- **No history / chat persistence.** Chat history lives in `ChatService` separately; same fix could apply but it's a different mutator surface and doesn't have the same "lost on every reload" bite. Ship the bigger win first.

## Test plan

- [ ] Roll a character. Reload the tab. Character is still there.
- [ ] Roll a character. Restart the dev server. Reload. Character is still there (hydrate path).
- [ ] In a fresh incognito window: empty server, no localStorage → boot lands on the "roll a character" sheet.
- [ ] Two tabs both signed in: roll character in tab A. Tab B's next render picks up the same character via storage event / next telemetry tick.
- [ ] Tab A is mid-question; tab B reloads and tries to hydrate — server's bucket already has a character, hydrate is rejected (`bucket-already-populated`), tab B catches up via normal GET.
- [ ] Reroll character in the sheet → snapshot drops; new character rolls clean; reload still shows the new character.
- [ ] Logout → snapshot drops; signing back in starts fresh.

> **Base branch:** `claude/api-key-localstorage` (PR #30). Will need to be retargeted to `main` after #30 merges.

author: acedatacloud-dev
body:
## Problem

On https://hub.acedata.cloud/chatgpt/conversations, audio cards (and the entity-card download link in general) render the raw i18n key `common.button.download` instead of a translated label.

Reported via screenshot showing a Suno-generated audio card whose download link reads `common.button.download` instead of "Download" / "下载".

## Root cause

[src/components/chat/EntityCard.vue](https://github.com/AceDataCloud/Nexior/blob/main/src/components/chat/EntityCard.vue#L15) uses `$t('common.button.download')`, but the key was never defined in `src/i18n/{en,zh-CN}/common.json`. Only `button.downloadAndroid` and `button.downloadIos` existed.

When a key is missing, `vue-i18n` falls back to printing the key string verbatim, which is what we see in the UI.

## Fix

Add a plain `button.download` entry to `src/i18n/en/common.json` and `src/i18n/zh-CN/common.json`:

- en: "Download"
- zh-CN: "下载"

Per project policy, only `en` and `zh-CN` locales are updated manually here. Other languages will be picked up by the translation CronJob on the next pass.

## Verification

- `python3 -c "import json; [json.load(open(f)) for f in ['src/i18n/en/common.json','src/i18n/zh-CN/common.json']]"` → JSON OK.
- After deploy, the audio/video/file card "Download" link on `/chatgpt/conversations` will render the localized string instead of the raw key.

## Summary

Consolidate the validate-tag / jsonschema-tag duplication in `internal/watcherconfig` so each constraint lives in exactly one place.

- Dropped `validate:"min=1"` from `Path`, `Name`, `WatchedPath`. A new `registerSchemaConstraints` helper in `internal/watcherconfig/validate.go` walks the watcher config struct types via reflection at validator construction time, extracts `jsonschema:"minLength=N"` constraints from string fields, and installs equivalent struct-level validators on the validator. Net effect: same runtime check, single source of truth (the `jsonschema` tag).
- Removed the `validMediaTypes` package var. Added `medialib.AllMediaTypes()` as the canonical list, used by both `MediaType.JSONSchema()` (for the schema enum) and `validateMediaType` (for runtime).
- Kept the `JSONSchema()` overrides on `MediaType`, `Interval`, and `CompiledRegexp` — they describe on-disk shapes that differ from Go shapes.
- Left `validate:"gt=0"` on `ScanInterval` alone; `Interval.UnmarshalYAML` already enforces positivity, but UnmarshalYAML is not one of the three locations the issue calls out.

## Schema diff

`make generate-schema` produces a byte-identical `schemas/watcher.schema.json` (verified with `git diff schemas/`).

- `TestNewValidator_MinLengthRulesEnforced` — confirms empty `Name`, `WatchedPath`, and `Output.Path` are rejected by the validator returned from `NewValidator()`.
- `TestRegisterSchemaConstraints_EmptyStringRule` — confirms a sample struct with `jsonschema:"minLength=3"` rejects shorter values.
- `TestRegisterSchemaConstraints_IgnoresNonStringFields` — non-string fields are skipped.

body:
**Utility code only — INTENTIONALLY UNWIRED.** No callers in the live system. The pack-store routes that will invoke this land in PR C. This PR ships the pieces with a real test fixture so the route work in C doesn't have to debug the parser at the same time.

Second of three PRs replacing the closed [#24](https://github.com/cenetex/app-ruby-high/pull/24). Sibling to [PR A](https://github.com/cenetex/app-ruby-high/pull/31) (per-session pack architecture); independent — both branch off main.

## What's here

### `src/content/anki/parse.ts` — the .apkg reader
Pure-JS (jszip + sql.js, both vendored — no native build). Extracts notes from the SQLite collection (`collection.anki2` / `.anki21`), splits the field separator, strips minimal HTML, returns `{front, back, deckName, noteId}` per card.

Edge cases handled clearly:
- non-ZIP bytes
- ZIP with no Anki collection
- `.anki21b` zstd format → tells the user to re-export with "Legacy support" enabled (we don't pull in zstd for this)

`sql.js` wasm path resolution probes `node_modules` across multiple parent layouts (source-tree vs tsup `dist`) and only commits to a candidate after `fs.stat` confirms the wasm exists. Falls back to sql.js's bundled location if no candidate matches.

### `src/content/anki/distractors.ts` — front/back → MC question
Tight prompt, JSON-only response, 3 distractors per card. Validates: 3 unique strings, none equivalent to the correct answer.

- Concurrency cap (default 4 in parallel) keeps the import fast without burning the user's quota.
- Per-card retry on parse failure (default 1).
- Cards we still can't generate for are skipped (UI shows "X of Y imported" later).
- Cost shape: ~$0.001/card with claude-haiku-4.5; a 50-card import is ~$0.05.

**FAIL-FAST ON AUTH ERRORS:** 401 / 403 from OpenRouter throws `FatalAuthError`. The first worker to hit it trips a kill switch the others see; the import bails instead of grinding through 50 futile calls. Without this, a bad API key burns the user's per-minute quota on a useless import.

### `src/content/anki/pack.ts` — `AnkiDeck` → `ContentPack`
The deck becomes a single faculty (one-teacher-per-deck shape).
- Pack id includes a 6-char base36 timestamp+random suffix so re-imports of the same deck name don't silently overwrite each other.
- Faculty accent color hashed from the deck name (deterministic but distinct) — multiple Anki packs in the channels rail won't all read as the same Sally Science blue.

## Tests (22 new, all passing)

**`anki-parse.test.ts`** (7 tests)
- 3 input-validation tests (non-ZIP, no Anki collection, .anki21b)
- 4 **end-to-end** tests using a programmatic `.apkg` fixture built with sql.js + jszip in-test: 5-card round-trip, HTML stripping, malformed-card skipping, empty-deck handling. **This is the missing E2E coverage the original draft didn't have.**

**`anki-distractors.test.ts`** (9 tests)
- Happy path (4 options, correct slot, faculty stamped)
- Skip on under-delivered distractors (< 3)
- Skip on distractor collision with correct answer
- Retry-on-parse-failure with `maxRetriesPerCard`
- **Fail-fast on 401, 403** (verifies queue isn't drained)
- 500 is per-card transient (other cards still complete)
- Concurrency cap honored

**`anki-pack.test.ts`** (6 tests)
- Happy path (deck → pack with valid bank)
- Pack id collision avoidance via `idSuffix`
- `faculty.id ↔ room.teacherId ↔ question.faculty` consistency
- Deterministic-but-distinct accent color from deck name
- `maxCards` cost cap respected
- `ContentPack` interface compatibility (all required fields present)

## What stays the same

**Zero production code paths changed.** No imports of this module from any existing service / route / viewer. `npm test` jumps from 146 → 168; build artifact size grows by ~38 KB (jszip + sql.js JS bridge — wasm loads on demand, not at boot).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [ ] Manual: app boots normally, no behavior change anywhere

## Next

**PR C** — Pack-store routes (`POST /packs/import-anki`, `POST /packs/active`) + viewer overlay + per-session pack ownership (the privacy fix #24 was missing). Will depend on PR A's per-session pack architecture being merged first.

author: llblab
body:
## Summary

This prepares `@llblab/pi-telegram` for the 0.5.0 release.

- Makes Telegram controls responsive and predictable: `/status` and `/model` now execute immediately instead of waiting in the prompt/control queue, and post-agent-end dispatch retries after pi settles back to idle.
- Migrates inbound attachment preprocessing to the shared command-template contract: `template` + `args` + `defaults`, ordered fallback chains, stdout-as-output, stderr-as-diagnostics, and no shell evaluation.
- Tightens runtime/domain ownership by removing the broad registration domain and moving registration surfaces to their owners: attachments, commands, lifecycle, and prompts.
- Cleans release docs/context, clears the backlog, and removes vendored repository-local agent skills in favor of global validation tooling.

## User-Facing Changes

### Queue And Controls

- `/status` and `/model` are immediate Telegram controls and no longer get stuck behind active generation.
- Synthetic model-switch continuation turns still use the control lane so a model switch can resume before normal queued prompts.
- `👍` / `👎` remain local Telegram queue operations only:
  - `👍` promotes waiting turns into the priority lane.
  - Removing `👍` returns the turn to normal ordering.
  - `👎` removes a waiting turn.
- Reaction priority applies to text, voice, files, images, and media groups.
- No pi `steer` behavior is introduced for Telegram reactions.
- Status wording now uses the concise `model` busy label.

### Attachment Handlers

Inbound attachment handlers now use command templates in `telegram.json`:

```json
{
  "attachmentHandlers": [
    {
      "type": "voice",
      "template": "~/.pi/agent/skills/mistral-stt/scripts/transcribe.mjs {file} {lang} {model}",
      "args": ["file", "lang", "model"],
      "defaults": {
        "lang": "ru",
        "model": "voxtral-mini-latest"
      }
    },
    {
      "mime": "audio/*",
      "template": "~/.pi/agent/skills/groq-stt/scripts/transcribe.mjs {file} {lang} {model}",
      "args": ["file", "lang", "model"],
      "defaults": {
        "lang": "ru",
        "model": "whisper-large-v3-turbo"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Built-in placeholders are intentionally minimal:

- `{file}` — full local path to the downloaded file
- `{mime}` — MIME type if known
- `{type}` — Telegram attachment kind such as `voice`, `audio`, `document`, or `photo`

If a matching handler fails, the next matching handler is tried. If all matching handlers fail, the original attachment remains available to pi as a normal local file reference.

## Migration Notes

Attachment handler configs should use `template`; old `command` configs should be updated before using 0.5.0.

```json
{
  "type": "voice",
  "template": "~/bin/transcribe {file} {lang}",
  "args": ["file", "lang"],
  "defaults": {
    "lang": "ru"
  }
}
```

For local file paths, use `{file}`. The previous extra aliases (`{filename}`, `{path}`, `{basename}`) are intentionally not part of the 0.5.0 attachment-handler surface.

## Internal Changes

- Removed the broad `registration` domain.
- Added focused lifecycle and prompt registration ownership.
- Moved outbound `telegram_attach` ownership into the attachments domain.
- Kept pi SDK imports centralized in the pi adapter and preserved the flat acyclic domain graph.
- Aligned the portable command-template documentation with `pi-auto-tools`.
- Removed vendored `.agents/skills/**` copies from the repository.

## Validation

- `npm run validate` — passed
  - `npm run typecheck` — passed
  - `npm test` — passed, 351 tests
  - `npm audit` — passed, 0 vulnerabilities
  - `npm pack --dry-run` — passed, 32 packaged files
- `evolve-context` validation — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

## Release Checklist

- [x] Package version is `0.5.0`
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` has the 0.5.0 release section
- [x] `BACKLOG.md` has no open items
- [x] README and docs are updated

body:
## Summary

Second blocker PR. Closes the **2 P0 open-redirect findings** from [docs/audits/01-security.md](./docs/audits/01-security.md). Without this fix, an attacker-crafted phishing link `/sign-in?callbackUrl=https://attacker.com` bounces the user to `attacker.com` after a legitimate sign-in.

## What lands

### `src/lib/safe-redirect.ts` (new)

- `safeRedirectTarget(url, fallback='/')` — clamps an arbitrary `callbackUrl` to a safe same-origin relative path. Falls back to `/` if it's off-origin, protocol-relative (`//evil.com`), an API route (`/api/...`), or contains whitespace/control chars.
- `isAllowedRedirect(url)` — exposed predicate for any future callsite.

### `src/app/(auth)/sign-in/page.tsx`

Server-side: `safeRedirectTarget(searchParams.callbackUrl)` is called once and threaded through `redirect()`, the `SignInForm` `callbackUrl` prop, and the `SsoButtons` `callbackUrl` prop. The raw param is never trusted again after entry.

### `src/app/(auth)/sign-in/SignInForm.tsx`

Client-side: re-validates with `safeRedirectTarget()` before `window.location.href = ...`. Defense-in-depth — the server validated, but never hand `window.location` an attacker-controlled string.

author: techieanant
body:
## Problem

After deploying v1.3.0, the container logs show repeated warnings:

```
Warning: Module type of file:///app/dist/database/migrate.js is not specified and it doesn't parse as CommonJS.
Reparsing as ES module because module syntax was detected. This incurs a performance overhead.
To eliminate this warning, add "type": "module" to /app/package.json.
```

## Root Cause

The Dockerfile production stage copies the root `package.json` (no `"type": "module"`) to `/app/package.json`. The backend is built as ESM (`format: 'esm'` in `build.js`), so Node.js defaults to CommonJS, detects `import`/`export` syntax, and re-parses every `.js` file.

## Fix

Copy `backend/package.json` (which already has `"type": "module"`) instead of the root `package.json` in the production stage.

## Verification

- Build, lint, format-check all clean
- The change only affects the Docker production image layout

author: wasab1kastike
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce the time a single interactive DB transaction holds locks by moving read-only/precomputation outside the long transaction. 
- Preserve idempotency and uniqueness gating for ticks while making write phases short and retry-safe. 
- Reduce long sequential per-fortress write paths to improve throughput and avoid long-running TX contention. 

### Description
- Reworked `processCycleTick` in `apps/web/src/lib/game/tick.ts` to remove the top-level long `db.$transaction` wrapper and perform deterministic reads and calculations using normal DB calls (`db.*`) before writes. 
- Preserved idempotency by performing a short transaction that claims the tick via `gameTick.create` and exits on unique-key (`P2002`) collisions. 
- Converted many sequential `update` calls into batched/chunked concurrent writes for per-fortress persistence using a chunk size of 25 and `Promise.all` to bound concurrency. 
- Kept write-critical operations explicit and isolated (e.g., fortress updates, `scoreEvent.createMany`, dwarf roll updates, attack-unit updates) and adjusted helper calls to use the non-transactional `db` client where appropriate to clarify transactional boundaries. 

### Testing
- Ran static type checks with `npm run typecheck`, which completed successfully. 
- Attempted `npm run build` prior to the refactor as an environment check; the build failed in this environment due to external Google Fonts fetch errors from `next/font`, which are unrelated to the logic changes in this PR. 
- Verified the modified file (`apps/web/src/lib/game/tick.ts`) compiles under `tsc` as part of the typecheck run.

author: marcusrbrown
body:
Empirical capture of GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.40 `--resume` and `--connect` JSONL behavior to crystallize the validation strategy for the v0.2.x continuity slice. Intentionally split from the planning PR so the evidence chain has its own focused review.

## What landed

- **`tests/fixtures/connect-mismatch.jsonl`** (18 lines, line 8 invalid by design). Real capture demonstrating that `copilot --connect=00000000-... --no-remote` silently ignores the target session and creates a fresh local one. Exit 0, empty stderr, no error event \u2014 only `result.sessionId` at session end reveals the divergence.
- **`tests/fixtures/resume-mismatch.jsonl`** (18 lines, line 8 invalid by design). Real capture demonstrating that `copilot --resume=00000000-...` creates a new session that **uses the requested UUID as its session ID** (per CLI help: *Start a new session with a specific UUID*). Not a silent fallback \u2014 by design.
- **`docs/research/copilot-cli-capabilities-2026-04-27.md`** gains \u00a710.12a (initial findings) and \u00a710.12b (follow-up confirming `--connect` without `--no-remote` behaves identically).

## Empirical conclusions

| Behaviour | Status under CLI 1.0.40 |
|---|---|
| `--resume=<known-uuid>` continues that session | \u2705 `result.sessionId` matches requested |
| `--resume=<unknown-uuid>` continues a session | \u2705 New session created **with that UUID as its ID** |
| `--connect=<id>` with `--no-remote` | \u26a0\ufe0f Always silent-fallback; new UUID assigned |
| `--connect=<id>` without `--no-remote` | \u26a0\ufe0f Same silent-fallback; even known recent IDs mismatch |
| Pre-`result` event carries `sessionId` | \u274c None across 7 captures |
| Clean attach error / stderr signal | \u274c None at any layer for any connect permutation |

## Side-findings

- `session.mcp_servers_loaded` fires **3\u00d7** in 1.0.40 (was 1\u00d7 in 1.0.34). Consumers should treat as ephemeral and idempotent.
- `user.message.data.transformedContent` reliably contains literal newline characters in JSON string values, breaking one-JSON-object-per-line parsing. The parser's existing `{ type: 'unknown' }` fallback handles it. Real-world repro now on disk in both new fixtures (line 8).
- `--share[=path]` is a **local markdown transcript export**, not a cloud-share primitive. CLI 1.0.40 has no remote-share flag.

## Implication for the continuity slice

The remote-control mechanism behind `--connect` requires an actively running, listening session (two concurrent processes). That cannot be replicated in the plugin's one-shot `-p` execution model. Recommend deferring `--connect` from the first slice and shipping `--resume`-only \u2014 plan amendments to follow as part of `ce:work` rather than as a separate planning PR.

## Verification

- 2 new fixtures + 2 doc updates; no source changes
- `bun run lint` clean; `bun run typecheck` clean
- All sensitive paths scrubbed to `$HOME` literal; one real session UUID replaced with synthetic stand-in; UUIDs not appearing in user-controlled state are left as-is per existing fixture convention
- Both fixtures contain the line-8 invalid-JSON case authentically; this matches CLI 1.0.40 output and exercises the parser's malformed-line fallback

No changeset (docs-only). Resolves the empirical-capture step the v0.2.x continuity plan called out as Unit 3a.

author: jblacketter
body:
## Summary

Wires Phase 28 Step B auto-export. With `TAGTEAM_STEP_B=1` set, every cycle write triggers a re-render of `docs/handoffs/<phase>_<type>.md` from the shadow DB. The `.md` becomes the canonical git-committable conversation log, replacing the `_rounds.jsonl` + `_status.json` pair after activation. Default-off — without the env var, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The plan went through six rounds of plan-cycle review with Codex (verbatim plan recorded in `docs/handoffs/phase-28-step-b-autoexport_plan_*`); the implementation review (also via the Codex shuttle workflow) caught one should-fix that was addressed before this PR opened.

## What's in the PR

- **`tagteam/dualwrite.py`** — `step_b_active()` reads `TAGTEAM_STEP_B` per call (no process cache, so a long-running watcher daemon picks up flag flips without a restart).
- **`tagteam/cycle.py`** — `_auto_export_cycle_md` hook runs after the existing shadow-DB helpers in all three cycle-write paths (`init_cycle`, normal `add_round`, AMEND early-return). Sentinel-aware: if `DB_INVALID` is set the hook skips render and emits an `auto_export_skipped_db_invalid` diagnostic. Render failures and exceptions emit `auto_export_failed`; nothing escapes the cycle write.
- **`tagteam/auto_export.py`** — `render_cycle_to_file` writes `db.render_cycle` output verbatim (newline normalization removed; verbatim is the spec). New `render_all_cycles_to_files` for repair/migrate callers that have independently proven DB validity (sentinel-bypassing).
- **`tagteam/repair.py`** — `rebuild_db_from_files_and_verify` extracted as a sentinel-independent primitive. `attempt_repair` calls it within its existing sentinel guard. When `step_b_active()`, successful repair bulk-renders all cycle markdown before clearing `DB_INVALID`; export failure keeps the sentinel set so backoff retries.
- **`tagteam/migrate.py`** — `migrate --to-step-b` activates Step B. Combines sources from `docs/handoffs/` + `.tagteam/legacy/` via tempdir, runs structured `_check_all_files` pre-check, rebuilds the DB, parity-checks, renders each cycle's `.md` (skipping if already byte-equal to `db.render_cycle`), then per-file moves legacy files to `.tagteam/legacy/`. Render failures abort that cycle's move; partial-move failures are recoverable on rerun via filesystem-driven state detection.
- **`tagteam/state.py`** — `state diagnose` handles multi-kind diagnostics via `entry.get("kind") or entry.get("event") or "seq_mismatch"` compat. Per-kind formatters; defensive fallback for unknown kinds.

## Tests

530 passed, 3 skipped (was 522 before rebase onto main). New file: `tests/test_auto_export_hook.py` covering flag off/on, init/add/AMEND hooks, DB-invalid skip diagnostic, render-false and exception diagnostics. Extended: `test_auto_export.py` (byte equality), `test_repair.py` (rebuild helper + Step B bulk render), `test_state_diagnose.py` (multi-kind dispatch + unknown fallback), `test_migrate.py` (happy path, idempotent rerun, drifted .md rerender, render-failure-aborts-move, partial-move-failure-recoverable, malformed-source-reports-file-inconsistent).

## Known follow-ups (non-blocking)

- Refactor `_rebuild_step_b_db_from_sources` and `rebuild_db_from_files_and_verify` to share a single rebuild path (probably `rebuild_db_from_files_and_verify(project_dir, *, extra_source_dir=None)`).
- Document the Step B repair-failure operator story in SKILL.md: a transient `.md` write failure during repair keeps `DB_INVALID` set; recover by fixing the FS issue and waiting for the next repair attempt; failure reason is visible via `tagteam state repair-db` (not `state diagnose`).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` → 530 passed, 3 skipped
- [x] `TAGTEAM_STEP_B=1 tagteam migrate --to-step-b --dir /path/to/test-project` happy path: cycles get `.md` files, legacy `_rounds.jsonl`/`_status.json` moved to `.tagteam/legacy/`
- [x] Re-run the same migrate command: idempotent, exits 0, no-ops
- [x] With `TAGTEAM_STEP_B=1`, `tagteam cycle add ...` updates the corresponding `.md` after each round; without the env var, no `.md` written
- [x] `tagteam state diagnose` renders any `auto_export_failed` / `auto_export_skipped_db_invalid` entries with clean per-kind formatting

## Summary
Completely refactored the Australia outage map component from a custom SVG-based visualization to a Leaflet-powered interactive map. This enables real geographic positioning of outages, improved interactivity, and better scalability for operational use.

## Key Changes

- **Map Engine**: Replaced SVG viewBox rendering with Leaflet.js map library, enabling true lat/long coordinate system
- **Coordinate System**: Migrated from schematic SVG polygon paths to real geographic coordinates (lat/lng)
  - State centroids now use proper latitude/longitude values
  - City pins repositioned with accurate geographic coordinates
  - Outage markers now render at actual incident locations (requires `lat`/`lng` fields in outage data)
- **Styling & Theming**: 
  - Dynamic tile layer switching between CartoDB light and dark basemaps based on palette
  - Injected CSS animations for outage pulse effects (replaces SVG animations)
  - City pin labels styled as Leaflet tooltips with monospace font
- **Marker Rendering**:
  - Outage severity indicated by circle marker size (scaled by customer count)
  - Optional pulse animation with staggered timing
  - Interactive popups showing detailed outage information (suburb, postcode, operator, cause, status, voltage)
  - City pins rendered as small dots with permanent labels
- **Interactivity**:
  - Click handlers on outage markers to select state
  - Popup windows with formatted outage details
  - Zoom/pan controls with constrained bounds for Australia
- **Removed Features**:
  - State polygon overlays (replaced by basemap)
  - Weather overlay visualization
  - Lat/long grid lines
  - State label aggregations
  - Ops-mode coordinate ticks
  - Hatching pattern for editorial variant

## Implementation Details

- Uses React refs to manage Leaflet map lifecycle and marker collections
- Tile layer swapped reactively when dark/light mode changes
- Marker updates triggered by outage data changes
- City pins conditionally rendered based on `showPins` prop
- Palette colors dynamically applied to markers and labels
- Map size invalidation on height/variant changes to ensure proper rendering
- Leaflet CDN link added to index.html

author: eliasss3990
body:
## Summary

Implementa el hardening del cliente HTTP del `RemoteFlagProvider` según ADR-1.

- **Body cap (M-05)**: lectura por `InputStream` con `maxResponseBytes` (default **10 MiB**); `ResponseTooLargeException` con `limit()` y `seen()`. Stream en `try-with-resources` → libera conexión al pool en happy path y en excepción.
- **Shutdown timeout (A-03)**: `shutdownTimeout` (default **5s**) separado del `requestTimeout`. `shutdown()` cierra `HttpClient` primero (cancela in-flight) y drena el scheduler con ese timeout.
- **HTTP version (A-06)**: enum `HttpVersion { AUTO, HTTP_1_1, HTTP_2 }`. AUTO deja ALPN para `https://` y fuerza HTTP/1.1 para `http://`.
- **Source-compat**: `RemoteProviderConfig` ahora tiene 13 args canónicos; overload de 11 args delega con defaults; constructor de 9 args `@Deprecated` intacto.
- `followRedirects(NEVER)` preservado (anti-SSRF).

## Refs

- ADR-1 `docs/adr/001-remote-http-client-hardening.md`
- Hallazgos: A-03, A-06, M-05
- Plan: `code-review-arquitectura/05-plan-ejecucion.md` PR 7

## Test plan

- [x] 82 tests verdes en `openflags-provider-remote` (incluye nuevos: `RemoteHttpClientTest` body excedido / forzado HTTP_1_1, `RemoteFlagProviderShutdownTest`, `RemoteProviderConfigCompatTest`)

author: r0shi
body:
## Summary

Phases 1–4 of the language-packs design — closes the silent French OCR recall regression that's been latent since PR #258.

**Headline:** French content can now actually be OCR'd as French. Today the worker passes `tesseract -l eng+fra` despite the bundle shipping only `eng + osd`, so French docs silently fall back to English-only OCR. With this PR, an operator enables French at `/admin/languages`, the download manager fetches `fra.traineddata` + `fr_core_news_sm`, and the OCR stage reads the preference + uses the right `-l` arg per doc.

| Phase | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Static `(lang, tool) → ArtifactSpec` map (real upstream SHA256s for French) + disk layout helpers | ✅ |
| **2** | Synchronous download manager (httpx.stream + atomic SHA-verified install) + `/api/languages` REST endpoints | ✅ |
| **3a** | `enabled_languages` preference plumbing on `PATCH /api/me/preferences` (validates, dedupes, always inserts `en` first) | ✅ |
| **3b** | `/admin/languages` System Settings page with per-tool install state + Enable/Disable toggle | ✅ |
| **4** | OCR stage reads enabled_languages + intersects with installed packs + builds `-l eng+fra` dynamically; new `documents.ocr_languages_used` column persists what was used | ✅ |

## Architecture highlights

- **Real SHAs only.** `download_artifact` refuses to install anything whose content hash doesn't match the static map. Placeholder SHAs would just produce confusing install-time errors, so the schema-validation test rejects them at test time.
- **Atomic installs.** Each download writes to a `.tmp` sibling and atomic-renames after SHA verification. Interrupted downloads leave a `.tmp` file but never a corrupt `.traineddata` for the next call to misinterpret.
- **English is always implicit.** The API normalises `enabled_languages` to always include `en` at index 0 — the backend, the OCR resolver, and the frontend Disable button all agree turning off English would silently disable OCR for every doc and refuse to do it.
- **Unified tessdata dir.** Tesseract's `--tessdata-dir` / `TESSDATA_PREFIX` only accept ONE path. The worker maintains `<lang_packs>/_tessdata/` with symlinks to both bundled (`eng`, `osd`) and per-language pack (`fra`) `.traineddata` files. Setup is idempotent and runs at worker startup.
- **Doc-ID enumeration mitigation** (carried over from #264): admin-required endpoints 403 before resource lookup so a non-admin can't enumerate language codes via 404 vs 403 differentials.

## Caller note

Existing English-OCR'd docs do NOT auto-reprocess when a new language is enabled — by design (multi-thousand-doc corpora make auto-reprocess prohibitively expensive). `doc.ocr_languages_used` is written from this PR forward; legacy docs have NULL, which the future "reprocess with new language" UI will use to detect candidates.

**Worker restart** is required to pick up newly-installed packs (the unified tessdata symlinks are populated once at startup). Documented in the UI and in the worker startup hook docstring.

## Tests

68 new tests:

- `test_languages_static_map.py` (8) — schema validation
- `tests/lang_packs/test_storage.py` (8) — disk layout
- `tests/lang_packs/test_manager.py` (16) — download/verify/remove against pytest-httpserver fixtures (no real network)
- `tests/lang_packs/test_tesseract_setup.py` (5) — unified dir + symlinks
- `tests/api/test_languages_endpoints.py` (17) — full REST surface incl. auth gates, idempotency, per-tool failure handling
- `tests/test_api_auth.py` (4) — `enabled_languages` validation/normalisation
- `tests/worker/test_ocr_languages.py` (16) — preference resolution + Tesseract arg generation + integration helper

Plus two existing migration test files got module-scoped teardown fixtures (they previously left the DB at their tested revision, which was fine when that WAS head — now there's a newer head and subsequent tests need it restored).

**504 passed total (+68 new), ruff clean, format clean, frontend type-check + lint + prettier clean.**

## Out of scope (in the spec, future PRs)

- spaCy NER per-language model loading (the download manager already pulls `fr_core_news_sm`; the worker side that loads on demand is the next PR)
- Per-doc reprocess affordance ("doc was OCR'd English-only, reprocess with French now?")
- Onboarding wizard "Languages" step
- Curated default-list expansion to ~25 languages (currently English + French; pattern is purely additive)
